locationsMap.name: Achaia
locationsMap.title: Roman province in southern Greece associated with [Corinth](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000058) and [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s ministry
locationsMap.description: Achaia was the Roman province covering southern Greece in the New Testament era, with [Corinth](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000058) as its principal city; [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) ministered there, and the churches of Achaia are addressed repeatedly in [Acts](book-key://ACT) and the epistles.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Southern Greece, especially the Peloponnese and adjacent mainland, in the Roman province of Achaia

locationsMap.name: Admah
locationsMap.title: city of the plain destroyed with [Sodom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000212) and [Gomorrah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000091)
locationsMap.description: Admah was one of the Cities of the Plain named alongside [Sodom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000212), [Gomorrah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000091), [Zeboiim](location-id://64ca2dba-3916-4ccb-b5fe-7cea31cd2590), and [Bela](location-id://6684b9dd-e756-4c52-bace-16acfd1cb1d6); Scripture remembers it as a city overthrown in divine judgment, but its exact site near the southern Dead Sea remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Ai
locationsMap.title: Canaanite city east of [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032) defeated by [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816)
locationsMap.description: Ai was a Canaanite city near [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032) in the hill country, remembered for Israel's initial defeat and later victory under [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816); it is commonly associated with et-Tell, though that identification remains debated.

locationsMap.name: Allonbachuth
locationsMap.title: oak near [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032) where [Deborah](name-id://8d540846-0f87-41c7-8c13-6fb3fb6cb89f), [Rebekah](name-id://d9f63818-b074-4f13-86e7-63f1fcc88b53)'s nurse, was buried
locationsMap.description: Allonbachuth, meaning "oak of weeping," was the tree below [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032) where [Deborah](name-id://8d540846-0f87-41c7-8c13-6fb3fb6cb89f) the nurse of [Rebekah](name-id://d9f63818-b074-4f13-86e7-63f1fcc88b53) was buried after [Jacob](name-id://23ed64d8-8458-49af-9b51-f578ab3262d9)'s return to the land; the biblical notice is brief, and no exact site has been securely identified.

locationsMap.name: Ammon
locationsMap.title: territory and kingdom of the Ammonites east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987)
locationsMap.description: Ammon was the territory of the Ammonites east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) River, centered on [Rabbah](location-id://8475db56-629d-4fb4-aefa-e0856f861d6e) and the upper [Jabbok](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000111) region in present-day Jordan; it appears throughout the Old Testament as both kin to Israel through [Lot](name-id://6100a889-934d-48cf-9f71-f36e524c7766) and as a recurring rival kingdom.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The highlands around modern Amman in northwestern Jordan

locationsMap.name: Attalia
locationsMap.title: Pamphylian port city from which [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) sailed after preaching in [Perga](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000180)
locationsMap.description: Attalia was a harbor city in [Pamphylia](location-id://9647773e-8975-42cf-bb5a-703b4fa0e050) on the southern coast of Asia Minor; after preaching in [Perga](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000180), [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) and [Barnabas](name-id://ba3667d2-9c64-4e6e-8836-beb53828cb13) went down to Attalia and sailed from there on the return of the first missionary journey.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Antalya in modern Turkey

locationsMap.name: Antioch
locationsMap.title: Syrian city on the Orontes where believers were first called Christians
locationsMap.description: Antioch on the Orontes was the great Syrian city that became one of the chief centers of early Christianity; believers were first called Christians there, and it served as the home church for [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) and [Barnabas](name-id://ba3667d2-9c64-4e6e-8836-beb53828cb13)'s Gentile mission.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ancient Antioch at modern Antakya in Hatay Province, Turkey

locationsMap.name: Antioch in Pisidia
locationsMap.title: Roman colony in [Pisidia](location-id://9ddcd442-e346-4092-a330-1883578433ac) visited by [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) and [Barnabas](name-id://ba3667d2-9c64-4e6e-8836-beb53828cb13) on the first journey
locationsMap.description: Antioch in Pisidia, also called Pisidian Antioch, was an inland Roman colony near modern Yalvac in Asia Minor where [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) preached in the synagogue, gathered Gentile hearers, and later endured persecution remembered in [Acts](book-key://ACT) and [2 Timothy](book-key://2TI).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The ruins of Pisidian Antioch near modern Yalvac in Isparta Province, Turkey

locationsMap.name: Antipatris
locationsMap.title: city on the road between [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) and [Caesarea](location-id://6e538552-c0de-4899-9ce1-31556e333ecf) where [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s escort lodged
locationsMap.description: Antipatris was a city in the [Sharon](location-id://e4a0da39-dd21-4734-890d-67d9359b8119) plain on the route from [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) to [Caesarea](location-id://6e538552-c0de-4899-9ce1-31556e333ecf), rebuilt and renamed by [Herod](name-id://851c25fa-9ece-487d-971a-b664a1364626) the Great; [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s escort brought him there by night on the way to Caesarea.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Afek near Rosh HaAyin in modern Israel

locationsMap.name: Arabia
locationsMap.title: broad desert region east and south of the Levant
locationsMap.description: Arabia in Scripture is a broad regional term for the lands of Arabian tribes and desert peoples east and south of the Levant; in later New Testament usage it can also denote Nabataean Arabia, and [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) says he went there after his conversion.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Arabian Peninsula and adjoining desert lands east and south of the Levant

locationsMap.name: Aram
locationsMap.title: region of the Aramean states centered in [Syria](location-id://f4fe75e3-4f92-4642-bf57-3d6a59931322)
locationsMap.description: Aram was the biblical region of the Aramean peoples north and northeast of Israel, centered in [Syria](location-id://f4fe75e3-4f92-4642-bf57-3d6a59931322) and extending into upper [Mesopotamia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000151); in the King James Version the name is often rendered as Syria, especially in references to [Damascus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000061) and the upper [Euphrates](location-id://0bdad9de-f6dc-4681-8a5a-54526382bc9f).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The region of modern Syria and adjoining parts of southeastern Turkey and northern Iraq associated with the Aramean states

locationsMap.name: Ashdod
locationsMap.title: Philistine city on the southern coastal plain and one of the five chief cities of [Philistia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000183)
locationsMap.description: Ashdod was one of the five principal Philistine cities on the southern coastal plain between Joppa and [Gaza](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000084); it appears in the ark narrative, in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)'s conflicts with [Philistia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000183), and in later prophetic judgments against the [Philistines](name-id://35245676-ecab-4457-84b4-cc81d8d63bff).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Ashdod, identified with the site of ancient Ashdod southeast of modern Ashdod in Israel

locationsMap.name: Ashkelon
locationsMap.title: Philistine coastal city and one of the five chief cities of [Philistia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000183)
locationsMap.description: Ashkelon was a major Philistine city on the Mediterranean coast south of [Ashdod](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000020); it appears in the tribal border lists, in Samson's exploits, in [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)'s lament over Saul and Jonathan, and in prophetic oracles against [Philistia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000183).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Ashkelon, the archaeological site of ancient Ashkelon within modern Ashkelon in Israel

locationsMap.name: Assyria
locationsMap.title: upper Tigris region and imperial kingdom east of the Levant
locationsMap.description: Assyria was the Mesopotamian kingdom and homeland on the upper Tigris centered on cities such as Assur and Nineveh; in Scripture it became the great eastern empire that conquered the northern kingdom and repeatedly threatened [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Northern Iraq with adjoining parts of northeastern Syria and southeastern Turkey, corresponding to the Assyrian heartland and empire

locationsMap.name: Abana
locationsMap.title: river of [Damascus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000061) identified with the Barada
locationsMap.description: Abana was one of the rivers of [Damascus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000061) named by [Naaman](name-id://c1b2d0b5-e363-488d-a119-fcf0c74f3cfb); it is commonly identified with the Barada River, the chief river that waters Damascus and its surrounding oasis.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Barada River in and northwest of Damascus, Syria

locationsMap.name: Abarim
locationsMap.title: mountain range east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) including [Pisgah](location-id://2f1847ff-51c6-41d4-a74b-a9a1075e7cb0) and [Mount Nebo](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000157)
locationsMap.description: Abarim was the mountain range east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) and Dead Sea in the land of [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153), with [Pisgah](location-id://2f1847ff-51c6-41d4-a74b-a9a1075e7cb0) and [Mount Nebo](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000157) as its best-known heights; Moses viewed the Promised Land from this range, and Israel encamped there near the close of the wilderness journey.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Mountain range in western Jordan east of the Jordan Rift Valley and Dead Sea, including Mount Nebo and Pisgah

locationsMap.name: Abdon
locationsMap.title: Levitical city in [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797) allotted to the Gershonites
locationsMap.description: Abdon was a Levitical city in the territory of [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797) given to the Gershonites; Scripture mentions it only in the allotment lists, and its exact site is not securely identified.

locationsMap.name: Abel
locationsMap.title: shortened name for [Abelbethmaachah](location-id://859e6f75-0709-4662-8bff-ce85a36afbca) in the revolt of [Sheba](name-id://87da963f-c366-46e3-b16c-038dc798b0e5)
locationsMap.description: Abel is the shortened form used in [2 Samuel 20](chapter-key://2SA 20) for [Abelbethmaachah](location-id://859e6f75-0709-4662-8bff-ce85a36afbca), the northern city where [Joab](name-id://12ff519a-1af6-4374-bf58-09dbfb159d43) besieged [Sheba](name-id://87da963f-c366-46e3-b16c-038dc798b0e5) and the wise woman secured the city's deliverance.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell Abelbethmaachah near Metula on the Israel-Lebanon border

locationsMap.name: Abelbethmaachah
locationsMap.title: fortified northern city near [Dan](location-id://dadc79b1-e84f-40e0-ab31-2fa96b6ed4bd) and [Ijon](location-id://21a0cf02-051c-4f0e-a56f-b7a99f25aea2)
locationsMap.description: Abelbethmaachah was a fortified city in the far north of Israel near [Dan](location-id://dadc79b1-e84f-40e0-ab31-2fa96b6ed4bd) and [Ijon](location-id://21a0cf02-051c-4f0e-a56f-b7a99f25aea2); it was later struck by Ben-hadad of [Aram](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000015) and by Tiglath-pileser III, and is identified with Tell Abelbethmaachah near Metula.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell Abelbethmaachah (Abil el-Qamh) near Metula on the Israel-Lebanon border

locationsMap.name: Abelmaim
locationsMap.title: alternate biblical name of [Abelbethmaachah](location-id://859e6f75-0709-4662-8bff-ce85a36afbca)
locationsMap.description: Abelmaim is the name used in [2 Chronicles](book-key://2CH) for the northern city also known as [Abelbethmaachah](location-id://859e6f75-0709-4662-8bff-ce85a36afbca), which Ben-hadad attacked in Asa's day; it is identified with Tell Abelbethmaachah near Metula.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell Abelbethmaachah (Abil el-Qamh) near Metula on the Israel-Lebanon border

locationsMap.name: Abelmeholah
locationsMap.title: city in the Jordan Valley associated with [Elisha](name-id://6e9af9e4-8635-4289-826f-bf6d37611683)
locationsMap.description: Abelmeholah was a town or district in the Jordan Valley south of Beth-shean, remembered as [Elisha](name-id://6e9af9e4-8635-4289-826f-bf6d37611683)'s home and as a boundary in [Gideon](name-id://c639ae62-acde-4142-a3f5-fd40204fc455)'s pursuit of Midian; modern scholarship places it west of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) near the Wadi al-Malih area, but the exact site remains uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Area west of the Jordan near Wadi al-Malih south of Beth-shean

locationsMap.name: Abelshittim
locationsMap.title: last Israelite encampment in the plains of [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153) before crossing the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987)
locationsMap.description: Abelshittim, also called [Shittim](location-id://6bdcf892-9c79-4cce-b479-66ff40e31758), was Israel's last encampment east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) before the crossing under [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816) and is associated with the Baalpeor episode; it is commonly identified with the area of Tell el-Hammam and ancient Abila in the plains of [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Area around Tell el-Hammam and Abila in the plains of Moab, Jordan

locationsMap.name: Abilene
locationsMap.title: district northwest of [Damascus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000061) ruled by [Lysanias](name-id://a87151f1-14cd-4a07-aaad-d33de2fa8daa) in the time of John the Baptist
locationsMap.description: Abilene was a small district in the Anti-[Lebanon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000133) foothills northwest of [Damascus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000061), named from its chief city Abila Lysaniou; Luke places it under [Lysanias](name-id://a87151f1-14cd-4a07-aaad-d33de2fa8daa) at the beginning of John the Baptist's ministry.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: District around Abila Lysaniou at modern Souq Wadi Barada, northwest of Damascus, Syria

locationsMap.name: Accad
locationsMap.title: KJV form of Akkad, city of [Nimrod](name-id://80b191de-d8ed-486d-bbb5-bd36756496ac)'s kingdom in [Shinar](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000204)
locationsMap.description: Accad is the King James Version form of Akkad, one of the cities named in [Nimrod](name-id://80b191de-d8ed-486d-bbb5-bd36756496ac)'s kingdom in the land of [Shinar](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000204); it is generally connected with ancient Agade, though the exact archaeological site remains unknown.

locationsMap.name: Achshaph
locationsMap.title: royal Canaanite city in the territory later assigned to [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797)
locationsMap.description: Achshaph was a royal Canaanite city in northern [Canaan](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000045) whose king joined the coalition against [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816); the site later fell within the allotment of [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797), but modern identification remains debated, with Tell Keisan among the leading proposals.

locationsMap.name: Achzib
locationsMap.title: coastal city of [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797) on the Phoenician border
locationsMap.description: Achzib was a fortified coastal city assigned to [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797) on the Mediterranean between Acre and [Tyre](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000226), but the Asherites did not dispossess its Phoenician inhabitants; it is identified with Tel Achziv at the site later known as Az-Zeeb.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Achziv on the Mediterranean coast north of Acre in Israel

locationsMap.name: Adadah
locationsMap.title: town in the southern territory of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Adadah was a town listed among the southern settlements of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) toward [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064); it is mentioned only once, and its site is unknown, with some scholars suspecting the name may preserve a corrupted form of another place-name.

locationsMap.name: Adam
locationsMap.title: place on the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) near [Zarethan](location-id://4a49e23c-67ec-494f-96bf-f421751af5c2) where the waters stood still
locationsMap.description: Adam was the place near [Zarethan](location-id://4a49e23c-67ec-494f-96bf-f421751af5c2) where the waters of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) were cut off for Israel's crossing in [Joshua](book-key://JOS); its exact site is uncertain, and some scholars have even suspected the name reflects a textual problem rather than a secure toponym.

locationsMap.name: Adamah
locationsMap.title: fortified city of [Naphtali](name-id://e8c79c45-33b0-4b1e-9265-368c54b9604a)
locationsMap.description: Adamah was one of the fortified cities of [Naphtali](name-id://e8c79c45-33b0-4b1e-9265-368c54b9604a) named in Joshua's allotment list; a location west of [Tiberias](location-id://8e5502fe-336a-4263-b9a2-2f31ee57e754) has been proposed, but no identification is secure.

locationsMap.name: Adami Nekeb
locationsMap.title: frontier pass on the border of [Naphtali](name-id://e8c79c45-33b0-4b1e-9265-368c54b9604a)
locationsMap.description: Adami Nekeb, rendered Adami-hannekeb in some versions, was a frontier point on the border of [Naphtali](name-id://e8c79c45-33b0-4b1e-9265-368c54b9604a); the name appears to describe 'the pass of Adami,' and while identifications such as Damieh west of [Tiberias](location-id://8e5502fe-336a-4263-b9a2-2f31ee57e754) have been proposed, the site remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Adithaim
locationsMap.title: Shephelah town in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Adithaim was a town in the Shephelah of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) named only in Joshua's town list; no secure modern identification has been established.

locationsMap.name: Adoraim
locationsMap.title: fortified town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) later known as Dura
locationsMap.description: Adoraim was one of the fortified towns strengthened by [Rehoboam](name-id://68d5eac0-52b9-4b0b-b484-8c7b5c3b8971) in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119); it is identified with modern Dura southwest of [Hebron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000103).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Dura, southwest of Hebron in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Adramyttium
locationsMap.title: Aeolian port city whose ship carried [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) from [Caesarea](location-id://6e538552-c0de-4899-9ce1-31556e333ecf)
locationsMap.description: Adramyttium was a port city of Aeolis in northwestern Asia Minor; [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) embarked on a ship of Adramyttium at [Caesarea](location-id://6e538552-c0de-4899-9ce1-31556e333ecf) on the voyage that eventually led toward [Rome](location-id://ff427d76-a9e7-4a50-bc2d-61b6b459e87b).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Site near modern Oren/Burhaniye in Balikesir Province, Turkey

locationsMap.name: Adullam
locationsMap.title: Canaanite and Judean town in the Shephelah associated with [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)'s cave
locationsMap.description: Adullam was a town in the Judean Shephelah near the [Valley of Elah](location-id://29f276d2-7c8e-4f2d-b8fc-1e42a5d2d893), famous for the cave where [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) took refuge; it is usually identified with Khirbet ʿAid el-Miyeh or nearby Khirbet esh-Sheikh Madhkur, though the precise point remains debated.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Khirbet ʿAid el-Miyeh / Khirbet esh-Sheikh Madhkur in the Judean Shephelah

locationsMap.name: Adummim
locationsMap.title: ascent on the road from [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) to [Jericho](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000116)
locationsMap.description: Adummim was the ascent or pass on the desert road between [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) and [Jericho](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000116), on the south side of Wadi Qelt; the route is well known, but the exact biblical referent within the pass is not entirely certain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tal'at ed-Dumm / the ascent above Wadi Qelt on the Jerusalem-Jericho road in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Aenon
locationsMap.title: site near [Salim](location-id://9b2f493d-b1e9-4074-b33e-4f48c7baf1e7) where John baptized because there was much water
locationsMap.description: Aenon near [Salim](location-id://9b2f493d-b1e9-4074-b33e-4f48c7baf1e7) was the place mentioned in [John](book-key://JHN) where John the Baptist continued baptizing; several locations with abundant springs have been proposed, especially near Tell Shalem in the Jordan Valley and at ʿAinun in Wadi Far'a, so the site remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Ahava
locationsMap.title: canal or river in [Babylon](location-id://8939f721-e16f-4837-84f0-ec3dcc65ea70) where Ezra gathered the returnees
locationsMap.description: Ahava was the canal or river in [Babylon](location-id://8939f721-e16f-4837-84f0-ec3dcc65ea70) where Ezra assembled exiles, proclaimed a fast, and began the journey to [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117); its location is unknown, though some interpreters have thought the name may refer both to a watercourse and to a settlement beside it.

locationsMap.name: Ahlab
locationsMap.title: town in [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797) from which the Canaanite inhabitants were not expelled
locationsMap.description: Ahlab was one of the northern towns assigned to [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797) whose inhabitants the tribe did not drive out in the period of the Judges; its exact site is uncertain, though it belonged to the Phoenician-facing belt of Asherite settlements.

locationsMap.name: Aiath
locationsMap.title: Isaianic form of [Ai](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004) in [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef)
locationsMap.description: Aiath is the form of [Ai](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004) used in Isaiah's march oracle, referring to the hill-country town east of [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032) remembered from Joshua's conquest narratives; it is generally identified with Ai, though the exact archaeological correlation remains debated.

locationsMap.name: Aija
locationsMap.title: postexilic form of [Ai](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004) resettled by Benjamites
locationsMap.description: Aija is the form of [Ai](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004) used in Nehemiah's list of Benjaminite settlements after the exile, referring to the same town east of [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032) known elsewhere as Ai or [Aiath](location-id://d7864089-1ffc-4fc5-a6f7-d541f95f5ba0); its exact archaeological identification remains debated.

locationsMap.name: Aijalon
locationsMap.title: Levitical town and valley gateway on the western approach to [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: Aijalon was a town on the borderland of [Dan](name-id://3de74a0e-f0c6-4087-b902-c30a6d218cff) later associated with [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef), famous for Joshua's battle, the valley bearing its name, and later defensive importance under the kings of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119); it is commonly identified with Yalo in the Ayalon Valley.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Yalo in the Ayalon Valley, near modern Canada Park in Israel

locationsMap.name: Ain
locationsMap.title: town in the Negev allotted to [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and later Simeon
locationsMap.description: Ain was a southern town in the Negev first listed with [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and later counted within Simeon's inheritance; it also appears among the Levitical towns, but its exact site remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Akrabbim
locationsMap.title: Scorpions Pass on the southern border of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Akrabbim, more fully the ascent of Akrabbim, was the steep pass on the southern frontier of [Canaan](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000045) and [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) toward the [Arabah](location-id://bfd23a68-b7bd-4bd0-99fe-d1d16a0b2a71) and [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064); it is commonly connected with modern Ma'ale Akrabbim, though the precise biblical line remains debated.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Modern Ma'ale Akrabbim in the Negev of southern Israel

locationsMap.name: Alemeth
locationsMap.title: Chronicles form of the Levitical town also called [Almon](location-id://18e003a2-933e-43f5-9755-a2301fcc54a3)
locationsMap.description: Alemeth is the name used in Chronicles for the Benjaminite Levitical town called [Almon](location-id://18e003a2-933e-43f5-9755-a2301fcc54a3) in [Joshua](book-key://JOS); it is commonly associated with the vicinity of modern Almon or Khirbet Almit northeast of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117), though the exact identification is not certain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Vicinity of Khirbet Almit northeast of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Alexandria
locationsMap.title: great Egyptian port city represented in [Acts](book-key://ACT) by [Apollos](name-id://dfbdaf3b-209b-43ca-8d2e-ba173fabb415) and Alexandrian grain ships
locationsMap.description: Alexandria was the major Hellenistic and Roman port of [Egypt](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000065), known in the New Testament as the home city of [Apollos](name-id://dfbdaf3b-209b-43ca-8d2e-ba173fabb415) and the registry port of the Alexandrian grain ships that carried [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) toward [Rome](location-id://ff427d76-a9e7-4a50-bc2d-61b6b459e87b).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Alexandria in modern Egypt

locationsMap.name: Allonbachuth
locationsMap.title: KJV form of Allonbachuth, the oak below [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032) where [Deborah](name-id://8d540846-0f87-41c7-8c13-6fb3fb6cb89f) was buried
locationsMap.description: Allonbachuth is the King James Version spelling of Allonbachuth, the "oak of weeping" below [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032) where [Deborah](name-id://8d540846-0f87-41c7-8c13-6fb3fb6cb89f), [Rebekah](name-id://d9f63818-b074-4f13-86e7-63f1fcc88b53)'s nurse, was buried; the exact site is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Almon
locationsMap.title: Joshua form of the Levitical town also called [Alemeth](location-id://cdd88429-0409-43ab-acb6-2d098554ac38)
locationsMap.description: Almon is the Joshua form of the Benjaminite Levitical town called [Alemeth](location-id://cdd88429-0409-43ab-acb6-2d098554ac38) in Chronicles; it is usually sought in the vicinity of Khirbet Almit northeast of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117), though the identification is not certain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Vicinity of Khirbet Almit northeast of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Almondiblathaim
locationsMap.title: encampment in [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153) before the mountains of [Abarim](location-id://69302e1c-c9d3-4416-8732-643fd7f51064)
locationsMap.description: Almondiblathaim was one of Israel's wilderness encampments in the plains of [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153) shortly before the ascent to the mountains of [Abarim](location-id://69302e1c-c9d3-4416-8732-643fd7f51064); its precise location remains unknown.

locationsMap.name: Alush
locationsMap.title: wilderness encampment between Dophkah and Rephidim
locationsMap.description: Alush was one of the wilderness stations on Israel's route between Dophkah and Rephidim in the [Sinai](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000210) itinerary; no secure modern site has been identified.

locationsMap.name: Amad
locationsMap.title: Asherite town in the western [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080)
locationsMap.description: Amad was a town in the allotment of [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797) named in the tribal boundary list of Joshua; no secure modern identification has been established.

locationsMap.name: Amam
locationsMap.title: southern town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) toward [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064)
locationsMap.description: Amam was one of the southern settlements of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) listed toward the border with [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064); it is mentioned only in the town list, and its exact site remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Amana
locationsMap.title: Anti-[Lebanon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000133) height named in the [Song of Solomon](book-key://SNG)
locationsMap.description: Amana is the mountain or mountain range named with [Lebanon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000133), [Senir](location-id://979ef039-2ab8-424c-9cee-32a507c0695a), and [Hermon](location-id://9ed57141-d70e-475b-b75f-a72a0f541a48) in the [Song of Solomon](book-key://SNG), usually taken as a height in the Anti-Lebanon region above [Damascus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000061); the precise summit intended is uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: A peak or ridge in the Anti-Lebanon range above Damascus, often associated with Jabal az-Zabadani or nearby heights

locationsMap.name: Ammah
locationsMap.title: hill near [Gibeon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000088) on the pursuit route after the battle by the pool
locationsMap.description: Ammah was the hill reached in the pursuit toward the wilderness after [Abner](name-id://3ce44295-3e16-47da-9037-8888f703aae7) and [Joab](name-id://12ff519a-1af6-4374-bf58-09dbfb159d43)'s battle by [Gibeon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000088); the site is not securely identified.

locationsMap.name: Amphipolis
locationsMap.title: Macedonian city on the Via Egnatia visited on [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s journey
locationsMap.description: Amphipolis was a prominent city of [Macedonia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000139) on the Via Egnatia between [Philippi](location-id://b9e3c9b4-d890-4ba6-b440-1d71b3ff8143) and [Thessalonica](location-id://b6bc0597-c58a-450e-8681-3c7e39704491); [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) and [Silas](name-id://1879776a-c64b-4e0b-9a88-f920b35d9efb) passed through it on the way to Thessalonica.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Amphipoli in modern Greece

locationsMap.name: Anab
locationsMap.title: hill-country town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) associated with the Anakim
locationsMap.description: Anab was a town in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119), remembered as one of the places from which [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816) cut off the Anakim; it is commonly identified with Khirbet Anab southwest of [Hebron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000103).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Khirbet Anab southwest of Hebron in the southern West Bank

locationsMap.name: Anaharath
locationsMap.title: town of [Issachar](name-id://380b2749-91f8-4a15-bcc2-0da2476c025b) in the [Jezreel](location-id://01fb54a8-39da-4de4-9ba9-6c91d7efff5b) region
locationsMap.description: Anaharath was a town in the allotment of [Issachar](name-id://380b2749-91f8-4a15-bcc2-0da2476c025b) in the [Jezreel](location-id://01fb54a8-39da-4de4-9ba9-6c91d7efff5b) region; proposed identifications exist, but no site is securely established.

locationsMap.name: Ananiah
locationsMap.title: postexilic Benjaminite settlement north of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: Ananiah was a Benjaminite settlement reoccupied after the exile and listed with Nob and Anathoth; it is commonly connected with the area of modern Beit Hanina, though the identification is not certain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Commonly associated with modern Beit Hanina north of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Anathoth
locationsMap.title: priestly town in [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) and home of [Jeremiah](name-id://3a62ca29-870f-4a9b-844b-887f828a0cd5)
locationsMap.description: Anathoth was a priestly town in [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) northeast of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117), remembered as the home of [Abiathar](name-id://514e3122-212b-4714-b2c0-f1c6623ef5d6) and especially of the prophet [Jeremiah](name-id://3a62ca29-870f-4a9b-844b-887f828a0cd5); it is identified with modern Anata.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Anata northeast of Jerusalem in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Anem
locationsMap.title: Levitical town in [Issachar](name-id://380b2749-91f8-4a15-bcc2-0da2476c025b) possibly corresponding to En-gannim
locationsMap.description: Anem was a Levitical town of [Issachar](name-id://380b2749-91f8-4a15-bcc2-0da2476c025b) named in Chronicles and is often taken to correspond to En-gannim in the parallel list of Joshua; its exact site remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Aner
locationsMap.title: Levitical town in western [Manasseh](name-id://6d826bc2-ac80-4c27-af89-258a50f37dfe)
locationsMap.description: Aner was a Levitical town in the territory of western [Manasseh](name-id://6d826bc2-ac80-4c27-af89-258a50f37dfe) and is sometimes connected with [Taanach](location-id://e7ae9ccc-c2ef-4ee6-9e90-b422084a6c7b) in the parallel Joshua tradition, though the correlation is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Anim
locationsMap.title: hill-country town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Anim was a town in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) listed among the southern settlements; no secure modern identification has been established.

locationsMap.name: Aphek
locationsMap.title: city in the [Sharon](location-id://e4a0da39-dd21-4734-890d-67d9359b8119) plain where Israel fought the [Philistines](name-id://35245676-ecab-4457-84b4-cc81d8d63bff)
locationsMap.description: Aphek was a city in the [Sharon](location-id://e4a0da39-dd21-4734-890d-67d9359b8119) plain, commonly identified with Tel Aphek near [Antipatris](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000013), where Israel camped against the [Philistines](name-id://35245676-ecab-4457-84b4-cc81d8d63bff) in Samuel and which may also be the Aphek listed among Joshua's defeated kings.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Aphek at Antipatris near Rosh HaAyin in Israel

locationsMap.name: Aphekah
locationsMap.title: hill-country town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Aphekah was a town in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) mentioned in Joshua's list; its exact site is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Aphik
locationsMap.title: northern Phoenician-border city in [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797), variant of [Aphek](location-id://46d234fa-f572-4af0-abce-a44da6c29f4e)
locationsMap.description: Aphik is the form used in [Judges](book-key://JDG) for the northern city on [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797)'s frontier with the Phoenicians, corresponding to the [Aphek](location-id://46d234fa-f572-4af0-abce-a44da6c29f4e) named in [Joshua](book-key://JOS); it is often associated with Afqa in [Lebanon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000133), though the identification is debated.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Often associated with Afqa in Lebanon

locationsMap.name: Apollonia
locationsMap.title: Macedonian city between [Amphipolis](location-id://c9a6278a-643c-431c-922b-c6d416db8497) and [Thessalonica](location-id://b6bc0597-c58a-450e-8681-3c7e39704491)
locationsMap.description: Apollonia was a city on the Via Egnatia in [Macedonia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000139) between [Amphipolis](location-id://c9a6278a-643c-431c-922b-c6d416db8497) and [Thessalonica](location-id://b6bc0597-c58a-450e-8681-3c7e39704491), mentioned on [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s route westward.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Nea Apollonia area in modern Greece

locationsMap.name: Ar
locationsMap.title: chief city of [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153) on or near the [Arnon](location-id://255578cb-f276-46f2-b857-683990b50518)
locationsMap.description: Ar, often called Ar of [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153), was a principal Moabite city associated with the [Arnon](location-id://255578cb-f276-46f2-b857-683990b50518) frontier; its exact site is uncertain, though it belonged to the gorge region north of Moab's plateau.

locationsMap.name: Arabah
locationsMap.title: great rift valley from the [Sea of Chinnereth](location-id://30d68225-3355-4ec2-9d41-8ba27a817d53) to the Gulf of Aqaba
locationsMap.description: The Arabah is the great depression of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) Rift, including the Jordan Valley, the basin of the [Salt Sea](location-id://2882f5a5-375a-40b9-9142-55341e8b6a91), and the southern stretch toward the Gulf of Aqaba; in Scripture it functions as a broad topographic region rather than a single town.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Jordan Rift Valley, especially the Jordan Valley and the southern Arabah

locationsMap.name: Arab
locationsMap.title: hill-country town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Arab was a town in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) mentioned in Joshua's settlement list; its precise site is uncertain, though proposals place it in the [Hebron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000103) region.

locationsMap.name: Arad
locationsMap.title: Canaanite city and kingdom in the Negev
locationsMap.description: Arad was the Canaanite city and surrounding kingdom in the Negev whose king fought Israel during the wilderness period; the site is identified with Tel Arad.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Arad in the Negev of modern Israel

locationsMap.name: Ararat
locationsMap.title: kingdom region of Urartu in the Armenian highlands
locationsMap.description: Ararat in Scripture is the kingdom region known historically as Urartu in the Armenian highlands; the ark came to rest on its mountains, and fugitives later fled there from [Assyria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000023).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Armenian highlands corresponding to the ancient kingdom of Urartu

locationsMap.name: Areopagus
locationsMap.title: rocky hill and council site at [Athens](location-id://7279824a-0cb1-40a4-86a2-8022707cd0fa)
locationsMap.description: The Areopagus was the rocky hill beside the Athenian acropolis and the name of the council associated with it; [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) addressed listeners there when he proclaimed the unknown God.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Areopagus Hill in Athens, Greece

locationsMap.name: Argob
locationsMap.title: rugged district of [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d) with many fortified towns
locationsMap.description: Argob was the rugged district of [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d) famous for its many fortified towns, commonly identified with the basaltic Lejah region of southern [Syria](location-id://f4fe75e3-4f92-4642-bf57-3d6a59931322).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Lejah basalt region in southern Syria

locationsMap.name: Ariel
locationsMap.title: poetic name for [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) in [Isaiah](book-key://ISA)
locationsMap.description: Ariel is the poetic name applied to [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) in [Isaiah 29](chapter-key://ISA 29), the city where [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) dwelt and which the prophet warns before its deliverance.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Armageddon
locationsMap.title: symbolic gathering place whose name evokes [Megiddo](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000148)
locationsMap.description: Armageddon, from the Hebrew Har-[Megiddo](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000148), is the symbolic place of mustering for the kings of the earth in [Revelation](book-key://REV); it is traditionally connected with Megiddo, though the exact referent is theological and debated rather than a securely mapped battlefield site.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Traditionally associated with Megiddo and the plain below it in northern Israel

locationsMap.name: Arnon
locationsMap.title: river gorge forming [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153)'s northern frontier
locationsMap.description: The Arnon was the river and deep gorge that formed [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153)'s northern frontier and later the border with Amorite-held land; it is identified with the Wadi Mujib canyon flowing into the Dead Sea.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Wadi Mujib in modern Jordan

locationsMap.name: Aroer
locationsMap.title: city on the north rim of the [Arnon](location-id://255578cb-f276-46f2-b857-683990b50518) gorge
locationsMap.description: Aroer was the city on the north bank of the [Arnon](location-id://255578cb-f276-46f2-b857-683990b50518) that marked the southern edge of the Transjordanian territory taken from [Sihon](name-id://7aefa340-c02e-4e80-9ce5-24d4215f6341) and later held by [Reuben](name-id://82279de3-ec8f-482d-a58d-119054ecb790) or [Gad](name-id://0b987f5d-4e64-4b73-a3e2-7f6b47dd7f46); it is commonly identified with Khirbet 'Ara'ir above the Wadi Mujib.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Khirbet 'Ara'ir above the Wadi Mujib in Jordan

locationsMap.name: Arpad
locationsMap.title: Syrian city conquered by [Assyria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000023)
locationsMap.description: Arpad was the important city-state of northern [Syria](location-id://f4fe75e3-4f92-4642-bf57-3d6a59931322) that fell to [Assyria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000023) and is repeatedly cited by the prophets as an example of conquered power; it is identified with Tell Rifaat north of Aleppo.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell Rifaat in northern Syria

locationsMap.name: Arumah
locationsMap.title: place near [Shechem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000201) where [Abimelech](name-id://eba375fa-1ab3-473b-85e6-f85f0771669c) stayed
locationsMap.description: Arumah was the place near [Shechem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000201) where [Abimelech](name-id://eba375fa-1ab3-473b-85e6-f85f0771669c) stayed during the revolt narrative in [Judges](book-key://JDG); it is often associated with Khirbet el-'Ormeh southeast of Nablus, though not with full certainty.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Often associated with Khirbet el-'Ormeh southeast of Nablus in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Arvad
locationsMap.title: Phoenician island city on the Syrian coast
locationsMap.description: Arvad was the Phoenician island city off the Syrian coast whose mariners and soldiers are mentioned in Ezekiel's lament over [Tyre](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000226); it is identified with modern Arwad.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Arwad Island off the Syrian coast

locationsMap.name: Ashan
locationsMap.title: town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) later reckoned to Simeon and given to the Levites
locationsMap.description: Ashan was a town in the south of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) later counted within Simeon's inheritance and assigned to the Levites; its exact location is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Ashnah
locationsMap.title: Shephelah town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Ashnah was a town in the Shephelah of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) listed among the lowland settlements; its site remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Ashtaroth
locationsMap.title: royal city of [Og](name-id://4c740990-dad3-4d94-b039-f55ed02efa7b) in [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d)
locationsMap.description: Ashtaroth was a royal city of [Og](name-id://4c740990-dad3-4d94-b039-f55ed02efa7b) king of [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d) and later a Levitical city in [Manasseh](name-id://6d826bc2-ac80-4c27-af89-258a50f37dfe); it is generally identified with Tell Ashtara in the Hauran.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell Ashtara in southern Syria

locationsMap.name: Ashteroth Karnaim
locationsMap.title: Bashanite city defeated in the days of [Chedorlaomer](name-id://ed428395-dc41-4ed2-9229-bd7abfaa930f)
locationsMap.description: Ashteroth Karnaim was the city or district of the Rephaim in [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d) defeated in [Genesis 14](chapter-key://GEN 14); it is closely related in name to [Ashtaroth](location-id://44a0699d-045b-487e-9c48-52f7a809bccb), but its precise site remains debated.

locationsMap.name: Asia
locationsMap.title: Roman province of western Asia Minor
locationsMap.description: Asia in the New Testament is the Roman province in western Asia Minor centered on cities such as [Ephesus](location-id://d0d9344d-8013-4dee-a125-bf3ca8d6810f), [Smyrna](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000211), and Pergamum, not the entire continent.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Western Asia Minor in modern Turkey, corresponding to the Roman province of Asia

locationsMap.name: Assos
locationsMap.title: harbor city of [Mysia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000163) visited on [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s return voyage
locationsMap.description: Assos was a harbor city of [Mysia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000163) in northwestern Asia Minor where [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) rejoined his companions after travelling overland from [Troas](location-id://a8c09279-58fd-483a-89e8-3af948752c58).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Behramkale on the site of ancient Assos in Turkey

locationsMap.name: Ataroth
locationsMap.title: Gadite town rebuilt east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987)
locationsMap.description: Ataroth was one of the towns east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) rebuilt by the tribe of [Gad](name-id://0b987f5d-4e64-4b73-a3e2-7f6b47dd7f46) in the land taken from [Sihon](name-id://7aefa340-c02e-4e80-9ce5-24d4215f6341); it is distinct from the Ataroth on the Ephraimite border.

locationsMap.name: Atarothaddar
locationsMap.title: boundary point on the border of [Ephraim](name-id://4ad1140c-2b95-4513-bd55-ed594805df5f) and [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef)
locationsMap.description: Atarothaddar was the boundary point on the border between [Ephraim](name-id://4ad1140c-2b95-4513-bd55-ed594805df5f) and [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) near lower [Beth-horon](location-id://1724eb98-7344-46c9-b069-6d0db1d09f5c); its exact site is not secure.

locationsMap.name: Athens
locationsMap.title: Greek city where [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) addressed the [Areopagus](location-id://434912d4-8733-4848-a0e0-a13a0f7363ba)
locationsMap.description: Athens was the leading city of classical [Greece](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000094) and the place where [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) preached at the [Areopagus](location-id://434912d4-8733-4848-a0e0-a13a0f7363ba) before moving on to [Corinth](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000058).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Athens in modern Greece

locationsMap.name: Atroth Shophan
locationsMap.title: Gadite town built east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987)
locationsMap.description: Atroth Shophan was one of the towns rebuilt by the Gadites east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) in the land taken from [Sihon](name-id://7aefa340-c02e-4e80-9ce5-24d4215f6341); its exact site remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Aven
locationsMap.title: derisive name for [Beth-aven](location-id://d1931ebf-e5b2-40e9-8548-328d554760f0) or [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032) in [Hosea](book-key://HOS)
locationsMap.description: Aven, meaning 'vanity' or 'wickedness,' is the shortened derisive name used by Hosea for the idolatrous sanctuary at [Beth-aven](location-id://d1931ebf-e5b2-40e9-8548-328d554760f0), closely associated with [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032).

locationsMap.name: Avith
locationsMap.title: Edomite royal city of [Hadad](name-id://b22c3d99-9e5b-4440-bb72-d9c3d880d111) son of [Bedad](name-id://1d3c55b3-8467-450e-938a-58019832c68f)
locationsMap.description: Avith was the city from which [Hadad](name-id://b22c3d99-9e5b-4440-bb72-d9c3d880d111) son of [Bedad](name-id://1d3c55b3-8467-450e-938a-58019832c68f) ruled [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064); its precise site is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Ava
locationsMap.title: city or district whose people were resettled in [Samaria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000196)
locationsMap.description: Avva was the city or district from which colonists were deported by the Assyrians to inhabit [Samaria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000196); its precise location is uncertain, though it belonged somewhere in the Mesopotamian sphere of Assyrian deportations.

locationsMap.name: Azal
locationsMap.title: place near [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) reached by the flight in Zechariah's vision
locationsMap.description: Azal was the place to which people would flee in Zechariah's prophecy of the cleft [Mount of Olives](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000158); proposals place it southeast of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117), but no identification is secure.

locationsMap.name: Azekah
locationsMap.title: fortified Shephelah town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) near the [Valley of Elah](location-id://29f276d2-7c8e-4f2d-b8fc-1e42a5d2d893)
locationsMap.description: Azekah was a fortified town in the Shephelah of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119), prominent in Joshua's campaign, the [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) and [Goliath](name-id://69bffebc-acde-4cc2-83a4-cc0533c60424) narrative, and the final defenses against [Babylon](location-id://8939f721-e16f-4837-84f0-ec3dcc65ea70); it is identified with Tel Azekah.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Azekah in the Judean Shephelah of Israel

locationsMap.name: Azmaveth
locationsMap.title: Benjaminite town also called [Beth-azmaveth](location-id://828904d8-ae88-4bd3-89ba-07ca3cccbc30)
locationsMap.description: Azmaveth was a Benjaminite town near [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117), also known as [Beth-azmaveth](location-id://828904d8-ae88-4bd3-89ba-07ca3cccbc30) in postexilic lists; its exact identification is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Azmon
locationsMap.title: southern border point of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) toward [Egypt](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000065)
locationsMap.description: Azmon was a landmark on the southern boundary of [Canaan](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000045) and [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) toward the Brook of Egypt; its exact site is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Aznothtabor
locationsMap.title: boundary point on the frontier of [Naphtali](name-id://e8c79c45-33b0-4b1e-9265-368c54b9604a) near [Tabor](location-id://0f233e04-9c83-4ca6-aaec-959c77bc98f9)
locationsMap.description: Aznothtabor was a boundary point on the frontier of [Naphtali](name-id://e8c79c45-33b0-4b1e-9265-368c54b9604a), apparently near the slopes of [Mount Tabor](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000160); no secure modern site is known.

locationsMap.name: Azotus
locationsMap.title: Greek form of [Ashdod](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000020) in [Acts](book-key://ACT)
locationsMap.description: Azotus is the Greek New Testament form of [Ashdod](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000020), the Philistine city on the coastal plain where [Philip](name-id://2d33a432-62de-4e66-a972-4d771b0e1a42) was found after baptizing the Ethiopian official.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Ashdod and the surrounding modern city of Ashdod in Israel

locationsMap.name: Appii Forum
locationsMap.title: market town on the Appian Way where brethren met [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)
locationsMap.description: Appii forum is the KJV form of the name of a town and road station on the Appian Way about forty-three Roman miles southeast of [Rome](location-id://ff427d76-a9e7-4a50-bc2d-61b6b459e87b), at the head of the canal that ran through the Pontine Marshes and the customary halt at the end of the first day's journey from the city. Brethren who heard of the apostle's approach came out as far as this place and [The three taverns](location-id://0873a885-e83e-4438-a9c7-20bd5515118c) to meet [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) as he travelled to Rome under guard, and when he saw them he thanked God and took courage ([Acts 28:15](verse-key://ACT 28:15)). The same site is entered in this dataset under its Latin form as [Forum of Appius](location-id://44ed0e35-10c0-4de5-b106-0ab01efe3794).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ruins near Treponti, Borgo Faiti, in Lazio, Italy

locationsMap.name: Asher
locationsMap.title: coastal tribal territory north of [Mount Carmel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000154)
locationsMap.description: Asher was the tribal territory allotted to the descendants of [Jacob](name-id://23ed64d8-8458-49af-9b51-f578ab3262d9)’s son [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797) as the fifth lot, stretching along the [Great Sea](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000093) from [Mount Carmel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000154) northward toward [Tyre](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000226). The tribe did not drive out the inhabitants of Accho, Zidon, and Achzib but dwelt among the Canaanites of the coast, and one of Solomon’s officers was set over Asher and Aloth.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: the coastal plain of western Galilee and southern Lebanon

locationsMap.name: Baalhazor
locationsMap.title: hill in [Ephraim](location-id://0e95bdcb-42ff-4f2a-80d7-00c32ac05b2c) where [Absalom](name-id://0e94a17b-69b1-4148-b7de-72eab8eea4cc) held the sheep-shearing feast
locationsMap.description: Baalhazor was the hill or estate near [Ephraim](location-id://0e95bdcb-42ff-4f2a-80d7-00c32ac05b2c) where [Absalom](name-id://0e94a17b-69b1-4148-b7de-72eab8eea4cc) held a sheep-shearing feast and killed [Amnon](name-id://7ddb908e-7d1c-4f3f-8acf-982a7042de76); it is often sought at Tell Asur northeast of [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032), though the identification remains uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell Asur northeast of Bethel in the central hill country of the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Babel
locationsMap.title: city in [Shinar](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000204) associated with [Nimrod](name-id://80b191de-d8ed-486d-bbb5-bd36756496ac)'s kingdom and the tower story
locationsMap.description: Babel was one of the chief cities of [Nimrod](name-id://80b191de-d8ed-486d-bbb5-bd36756496ac)'s kingdom in [Shinar](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000204) and is the biblical beginning of [Babylon](location-id://8939f721-e16f-4837-84f0-ec3dcc65ea70); [Genesis](book-key://GEN) also connects it with the confusion of languages at the tower.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The ruins of Babylon near Hillah in Iraq

locationsMap.name: Beersheba
locationsMap.title: KJV form of [Beersheba](location-id://0643b4cb-a5f4-4af3-b469-ed061976d1f4), southern city marking Israel's customary limit
locationsMap.description: Beer-sheba is the King James form of [Beersheba](location-id://0643b4cb-a5f4-4af3-b469-ed061976d1f4), the southern city in the Negev associated with [Abraham](name-id://4ce14dfc-b652-45d9-ac05-5f0cf716c412), [Isaac](name-id://a5b2f874-2008-4b28-9698-6357fe71c3bf), and later Judean life; 'from [Dan](location-id://dadc79b1-e84f-40e0-ab31-2fa96b6ed4bd) even to Beer-sheba' became a standard formula for the land's extent.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Be'er Sheva at modern Beersheba in Israel

locationsMap.name: Berea
locationsMap.title: Macedonian city whose synagogue searched the Scriptures daily
locationsMap.description: Berea was the Macedonian city where [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) and [Silas](name-id://1879776a-c64b-4e0b-9a88-f920b35d9efb) found hearers who received the word readily and searched the Scriptures; from there Paul moved on toward the coast and [Athens](location-id://7279824a-0cb1-40a4-86a2-8022707cd0fa).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Veria in northern Greece

locationsMap.name: Bethanath
locationsMap.title: fortified Naphtalite town whose Canaanite inhabitants remained
locationsMap.description: Beth-anath was one of Naphtali's fortified towns, but its Canaanite inhabitants were not expelled and instead remained under tribute among Israel.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Usually identified with modern Ainata or nearby sites in southern Lebanon

locationsMap.name: Bethany
locationsMap.title: village on the eastern slope of the [Mount of Olives](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000158) near [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: Bethany was the village east of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) associated with [Martha](name-id://d4efd460-a9bb-4b13-bf4f-be0722687197), [Mary](name-id://70aa6782-97ea-4d68-821f-749fbb81de14), and [Lazarus](name-id://56efde8a-d292-4505-887d-f86b7ee19ec8), and [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) regularly stayed there during his final visits to the city.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: al-Eizariya on the eastern slope of the Mount of Olives in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Bethabara
locationsMap.title: KJV place name for the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) site where [John](name-id://0def26d5-2ca4-4b89-95c1-f8d964d0c6e9) was baptizing
locationsMap.description: Bethabara is the King James reading for the place beyond [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) where [John](name-id://0def26d5-2ca4-4b89-95c1-f8d964d0c6e9) was baptizing in [John 1](chapter-key://JHN 1); the exact site remains uncertain and may preserve the name of a ford rather than a town.

locationsMap.name: Bethel
locationsMap.title: hill-country sanctuary town formerly called [Luz](location-id://e42b8f9d-964e-4478-9504-1fa698f80b49)
locationsMap.description: Bethel was the hill-country town north of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) where [Jacob](name-id://23ed64d8-8458-49af-9b51-f578ab3262d9) named the place after his vision, and later it became one of the chief sanctuaries of the northern kingdom.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Beitin in the central West Bank

locationsMap.name: Bethharan
locationsMap.title: one-word form of Beth-haran, Gadite town in the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) Valley
locationsMap.description: Bethharan is a one-word spelling of Beth-haran or Beth-haram, the Gadite town east of [Jericho](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000116) in the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) Valley later associated with Livias.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell er-Rameh and the area of ancient Livias in Jordan

locationsMap.name: Bethlehem
locationsMap.title: city of [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) identified with modern Bethlehem
locationsMap.description: Bethlehem was the Judean town south of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) associated with [Rachel](name-id://84d78b89-880b-4333-a822-9c8449f77fd0)'s burial nearby, the family of [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c), and the birth of [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab); Micah distinguishes it from the Bethlehem in Zebulun.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Bethlehem in the central West Bank

locationsMap.name: Bethrehob
locationsMap.title: northern town or district near Lebo-hamath
locationsMap.description: Bethrehob was a northern settlement or district near [Dan](location-id://dadc79b1-e84f-40e0-ab31-2fa96b6ed4bd) and Lebo-hamath; nearby Laish is described in relation to it, and Arameans from Bethrehob later served the Ammonites.

locationsMap.name: Bethsaida
locationsMap.title: Galilean fishing town associated with [Peter](name-id://2bcada1c-b00a-4214-8a2d-5a7b991f6641), [Andrew](name-id://6d793802-2fff-430a-b1a0-82be941453fc), [Philip](name-id://19fb4200-54fd-400d-805c-7a07d9e857e1), and [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab)'s miracles
locationsMap.description: Bethsaida was the fishing town associated with [Peter](name-id://2bcada1c-b00a-4214-8a2d-5a7b991f6641), [Andrew](name-id://6d793802-2fff-430a-b1a0-82be941453fc), and [Philip](name-id://19fb4200-54fd-400d-805c-7a07d9e857e1) and the place near which [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) fed the multitude and healed a blind man; the exact New Testament site remains debated.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: A debated site on the northeastern shore of the Sea of Galilee, most often et-Tell or el-Araj

locationsMap.name: Bethshemesh
locationsMap.title: Levitical town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) where the ark returned from [Philistia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000183)
locationsMap.description: Beth-shemesh was the Judean border town in the Sorek Valley where the Philistines returned the ark and where later kings of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) fought; it is identified with Tel Beth-Shemesh.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Beth-Shemesh near modern Beit Shemesh in Israel

locationsMap.name: Bochim
locationsMap.title: place of weeping where Israel lamented after the angel's rebuke
locationsMap.description: Bochim, 'weepers,' was the place where Israel wept and sacrificed after the angel of the LORD rebuked the nation; the exact site is not known.

locationsMap.name: Baal
locationsMap.title: Simeonite town in the south, probably a short form of [Baalath-beer](location-id://23b21934-66f4-4b65-a5f8-ca79d31f2796)
locationsMap.description: Baal was a southern Simeonite town or district listed in Chronicles; many interpreters identify it with [Baalath-beer](location-id://23b21934-66f4-4b65-a5f8-ca79d31f2796), also called Ramath of the south.

locationsMap.name: Baalgad
locationsMap.title: northern landmark at the foot of [Hermon](location-id://9ed57141-d70e-475b-b75f-a72a0f541a48) in the valley of [Lebanon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000133)
locationsMap.description: Baal-gad marked the northern extent of [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816)'s conquests, lying in the valley of [Lebanon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000133) under [Mount Hermon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000156) and associated with the region of Baal worship in the far north.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Usually sought in the Hasbani or Banias area at the foot of Mount Hermon

locationsMap.name: Baalhamon
locationsMap.title: place of [Solomon](name-id://509b7c2f-b8bf-4a4d-a393-550a7a4b259f)'s vineyard in the Song of Songs
locationsMap.description: Baal-hamon was the place where [Solomon](name-id://509b7c2f-b8bf-4a4d-a393-550a7a4b259f) is said to have had a vineyard in the Song of Songs; its location is unknown and the name may function poetically.

locationsMap.name: Baalhazor
locationsMap.title: spacing variant of [Baalhazor](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000024), [Absalom](name-id://0e94a17b-69b1-4148-b7de-72eab8eea4cc)'s estate in [Ephraim](location-id://0e95bdcb-42ff-4f2a-80d7-00c32ac05b2c)
locationsMap.description: Baalhazor is the spaced spelling of [Baalhazor](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000024), the estate or hill near [Ephraim](location-id://0e95bdcb-42ff-4f2a-80d7-00c32ac05b2c) where [Absalom](name-id://0e94a17b-69b1-4148-b7de-72eab8eea4cc) held the sheep-shearing feast and arranged [Amnon](name-id://7ddb908e-7d1c-4f3f-8acf-982a7042de76)'s death.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell Asur northeast of Bethel in the central hill country of the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Baalhermon
locationsMap.title: northern sanctuary or district associated with [Mount Hermon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000156)
locationsMap.description: Baal-hermon was the northern district or sanctuary associated with [Mount Hermon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000156), closely related to [Baal-gad](location-id://b140e0e2-3111-4244-b0b4-3d8580d0e980) and the far northern borderland of Israel's world.

locationsMap.name: Baalmeon
locationsMap.title: town east of the Dead Sea later known as Beth-meon or Ma'in
locationsMap.description: Baal-meon was the Transjordanian town allotted to Reuben and later reckoned to [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153); it is represented by other biblical forms such as Beon, Beth-baal-meon, and Beth-meon.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ma'in south of Madaba in Jordan

locationsMap.name: Baalpeor
locationsMap.title: sanctuary or locality associated with [Peor](location-id://479a8bc3-a004-4961-b621-109fa14b0b7d) above the plains of [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153)
locationsMap.description: Baalpeor was the Moabite cult-site or locality associated with [Peor](location-id://479a8bc3-a004-4961-b621-109fa14b0b7d), where Israel fell into idolatry and immorality before entering the land.

locationsMap.name: Baalperazim
locationsMap.title: battlefield west of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) where [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) broke through the Philistines
locationsMap.description: Baal-perazim was the place where [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) defeated the Philistines and named the site for the LORD's breaking forth like waters.

locationsMap.name: Baalshalisha
locationsMap.title: district that supplied firstfruits to [Elisha](name-id://6e9af9e4-8635-4289-826f-bf6d37611683)
locationsMap.description: Baal-shalisha was the district from which a man brought firstfruits to [Elisha](name-id://6e9af9e4-8635-4289-826f-bf6d37611683) during the famine; it likely lay in the central hill country west or northwest of [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032).

locationsMap.name: Baaltamar
locationsMap.title: place near [Gibeah](location-id://41084ab0-6cbc-4232-a844-fb8b405d97c3) in the Benjamite war
locationsMap.description: Baal-tamar was the place near [Gibeah](location-id://41084ab0-6cbc-4232-a844-fb8b405d97c3) where Israel set an ambush against Benjamin in the civil war narrated in [Judges](book-key://JDG).

locationsMap.name: Baalzephon
locationsMap.title: Egyptian frontier sanctuary opposite Israel's [Red Sea](location-id://26deae24-2471-47c1-8280-28e380224f20) encampment
locationsMap.description: Baalzephon was the place opposite Israel's camp before the crossing of the sea, probably an Egyptian frontier sanctuary or district near the northeastern Delta.

locationsMap.name: Baalah
locationsMap.title: alternate name of [Kiriath-jearim](location-id://c17c2d42-2618-4ff7-844d-247f21c0da32) on the [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)-[Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) border
locationsMap.description: Baalah is an alternate name of [Kiriath-jearim](location-id://c17c2d42-2618-4ff7-844d-247f21c0da32), the border town where the ark stayed before [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) brought it to [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Deir el-Azar / Tel Qiryat Ye'arim west of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Baalathbeer
locationsMap.title: Simeonite town in the Negev also called Ramath of the south
locationsMap.description: Baalath-beer was a Simeonite town in the south country identified with Ramath of the south; its exact site remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Baalath
locationsMap.title: Danite or Solomonic town in the lowland approaches
locationsMap.description: Baalath was a town assigned to Dan and later fortified by [Solomon](name-id://509b7c2f-b8bf-4a4d-a393-550a7a4b259f); it lay in the western lowland approaches toward the Philistine plain.

locationsMap.name: Babylon
locationsMap.title: great Mesopotamian capital on the [Euphrates](location-id://0bdad9de-f6dc-4681-8a5a-54526382bc9f) and symbol of imperial exile
locationsMap.description: Babylon was the great imperial capital on the [Euphrates](location-id://0bdad9de-f6dc-4681-8a5a-54526382bc9f) that conquered [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119), carried the people into exile, and became a dominant biblical symbol of pride, oppression, and judgment.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The ruins of Babylon near Hillah in Iraq

locationsMap.name: Babylonia
locationsMap.title: the wider Babylonian land and imperial region
locationsMap.description: Babylonia is the wider land of [Babylon](location-id://8939f721-e16f-4837-84f0-ec3dcc65ea70) in southern [Mesopotamia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000151), used in English to distinguish the region from the capital city itself.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Southern Iraq centered on the lower Euphrates and Tigris

locationsMap.name: Bahurim
locationsMap.title: Benjaminite village on the road east of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: Bahurim was the Benjaminite village encountered in the stories of [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)'s flight and return, lying east or northeast of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) on the route toward the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987).

locationsMap.name: Balah
locationsMap.title: southern town of Simeon also called Bilhah or Bala
locationsMap.description: Balah was one of the southern towns of Simeon in the Negev and is represented by related forms such as Bala and Bilhah in the tribal lists.

locationsMap.name: Bamothbaal
locationsMap.title: high place of Baal on the Moabite plateau
locationsMap.description: Bamoth-baal was the Moabite height or sanctuary listed among the Reubenite towns east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) and closely associated with Baal worship on the plateau.

locationsMap.name: Bamoth
locationsMap.title: height in the wilderness route above [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153)
locationsMap.description: Bamoth was the height named on Israel's wilderness route in [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153) and is closely related in tradition to [Bamoth-baal](location-id://09ea0cdf-c434-4726-a638-1f0ea4f98b20).

locationsMap.name: Bashan
locationsMap.title: fertile Transjordanian region north of [Gilead](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000089)
locationsMap.description: Bashan was the fertile highland region east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) north of [Gilead](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000089), famous for its cattle, forests, and the kingdom of [Og](name-id://4c740990-dad3-4d94-b039-f55ed02efa7b).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Hauran and Golan region of southern Syria and northern Jordan/Israel

locationsMap.name: Bathrabbim
locationsMap.title: gate or pool area at [Heshbon](location-id://fcdae541-01d2-47f8-a663-45a2f056a250) in the Song of Songs
locationsMap.description: Bath-rabbim is the gate or pool area at [Heshbon](location-id://fcdae541-01d2-47f8-a663-45a2f056a250) evoked in the Song of Songs; the phrase likely refers to a well-known city feature rather than a separate settlement.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: A city feature at ancient Heshbon, modern Tell Hesban in Jordan

locationsMap.name: Bealoth
locationsMap.title: southern town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) toward the Edomite frontier
locationsMap.description: Bealoth was one of the southern towns listed in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)'s Negev district toward [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064); its precise site is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Beautiful Gate
locationsMap.title: temple gate in [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) where the lame man was healed
locationsMap.description: The Beautiful Gate was the temple gate in [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) where the man lame from birth begged and was healed through [Peter](name-id://2bcada1c-b00a-4214-8a2d-5a7b991f6641) and John; its exact identification within Herod's temple complex is debated.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: A gate within Herod's temple complex, often associated with the Nicanor Gate in Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Beer
locationsMap.title: well in the wilderness where Israel sang after the princes dug it
locationsMap.description: Beer was the wilderness well where the LORD told [Moses](name-id://fff825ad-31e8-4843-a7dc-cd82e9878d73) to gather the people and where Israel sang after the princes dug the well with their staffs.

locationsMap.name: Beerelim
locationsMap.title: well or oasis on the wilderness route by [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153)
locationsMap.description: Beer-elim, 'well of the mighty ones,' was a stopping place on the desert route associated with [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153) in Isaiah's oracle.

locationsMap.name: Beerlahairoi
locationsMap.title: well in the south country associated with [Hagar](name-id://f90c700d-22eb-4853-88d7-7faca41ee81c), [Isaac](name-id://a5b2f874-2008-4b28-9698-6357fe71c3bf), and the Negev
locationsMap.description: Beer-lahai-roi was the well between [Kadesh](location-id://501d3b61-a4e6-4e1e-82b1-f8799fb77131) and [Bered](location-id://8bea3b37-c15c-4db5-a8e9-c9f624cabcc2) where [Hagar](name-id://f90c700d-22eb-4853-88d7-7faca41ee81c) encountered the angel of the LORD; [Isaac](name-id://a5b2f874-2008-4b28-9698-6357fe71c3bf) later dwelt by it in the south country.

locationsMap.name: Beeroth
locationsMap.title: Gibeonite town of [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) on the road north of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: Beeroth was one of the Gibeonite towns later reckoned to [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) and is remembered in the story of [Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb)'s assassins.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: el-Bireh north of Jerusalem is the common identification

locationsMap.name: Beersheba
locationsMap.title: southern city in the Negev associated with the patriarchs and [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Beersheba was the southern city in the Negev associated with [Abraham](name-id://4ce14dfc-b652-45d9-ac05-5f0cf716c412), [Isaac](name-id://a5b2f874-2008-4b28-9698-6357fe71c3bf), and later Judean administration, and it became the classic southern point in the phrase 'from [Dan](location-id://dadc79b1-e84f-40e0-ab31-2fa96b6ed4bd) to Beersheba.'
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Be'er Sheva at modern Beersheba in Israel

locationsMap.name: Beeshterah
locationsMap.title: Levitical town in [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d) usually equated with [Ashtaroth](location-id://44a0699d-045b-487e-9c48-52f7a809bccb)
locationsMap.description: Beeshterah was the Levitical town in [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d) allotted to the Gershonites and is commonly understood as another name or form of [Ashtaroth](location-id://44a0699d-045b-487e-9c48-52f7a809bccb).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Usually associated with Tell Ashtarah in southern Syria

locationsMap.name: Bela
locationsMap.title: older name of [Zoar](location-id://5d01ba7a-9112-460b-aea8-d80ada45bdc0) at the southeastern Dead Sea
