locationsMap.description: Bela was the older name of [Zoar](location-id://5d01ba7a-9112-460b-aea8-d80ada45bdc0), the small city at the southeastern Dead Sea remembered from the story of [Lot](name-id://6100a889-934d-48cf-9f71-f36e524c7766).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Zoar region at the southeastern end of the Dead Sea in Jordan

locationsMap.name: Beneberak
locationsMap.title: Danite town in the coastal plain
locationsMap.description: Bene-berak was one of the towns assigned to Dan in the coastal plain northwest of [Joppa](location-id://dd33c11c-6e8d-484a-8911-bb20e6126e7c).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Bnei Brak east of Tel Aviv preserves the ancient name

locationsMap.name: Benejaakan
locationsMap.title: wilderness station named for the children of Jaakan
locationsMap.description: Bene-jaakan was the wilderness station named for the children of Jaakan in the itinerary traditions of Israel's wandering.

locationsMap.name: Beon
locationsMap.title: short form of [Baal-meon](location-id://80dc92af-b077-4672-a9eb-a7fb7620ad83) in the Transjordan settlement list
locationsMap.description: Beon is the shorter form of [Baal-meon](location-id://80dc92af-b077-4672-a9eb-a7fb7620ad83) used in [Numbers](book-key://NUM) for the town east of the Dead Sea that later appears in Moabite and Reubenite contexts.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ma'in south of Madaba in Jordan

locationsMap.name: Bered
locationsMap.title: southern landmark near [Beer-lahai-roi](location-id://7bc0f8f8-6f4c-4ea5-b91e-020e944e79e4)
locationsMap.description: Bered was the landmark named with [Kadesh](location-id://501d3b61-a4e6-4e1e-82b1-f8799fb77131) in describing the location of [Beer-lahai-roi](location-id://7bc0f8f8-6f4c-4ea5-b91e-020e944e79e4) in the south country.

locationsMap.name: Berothah
locationsMap.title: northern border town between [Hamath](location-id://e88700f4-7b74-49f1-bf22-d4a4a6992b62) and [Damascus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000061) in Ezekiel's vision
locationsMap.description: Berothah was a northern border town or district named in Ezekiel's ideal frontier description and is probably related to [Berothai](location-id://e7ead3d6-fa5b-4940-bf66-9cb98999f550).

locationsMap.name: Berothai
locationsMap.title: Aramean city from which [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) took bronze
locationsMap.description: Berothai was the city from which [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) took much bronze from [Hadadezer](name-id://2d9ff281-73b3-4bd8-b94b-b414b234bce7) king of [Zobah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000246) and is probably the same place remembered as [Berothah](location-id://60a10e55-d5f7-4b73-bebf-74d560784ee5) in [Ezekiel](book-key://EZK).

locationsMap.name: Besor
locationsMap.title: brook in the Negev where [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)'s weary men halted
locationsMap.description: The Besor was the brook in the Negev where some of [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)'s men stayed behind while he pursued the Amalekites, and later where he divided the spoil.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Wadi Besor in the northwestern Negev

locationsMap.name: Betah
locationsMap.title: Aramean city of [Hadadezer](name-id://2d9ff281-73b3-4bd8-b94b-b414b234bce7) named with [Berothai](location-id://e7ead3d6-fa5b-4940-bf66-9cb98999f550)
locationsMap.description: Betah was the city named with [Berothai](location-id://e7ead3d6-fa5b-4940-bf66-9cb98999f550) among the places from which [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) took much bronze from [Hadadezer](name-id://2d9ff281-73b3-4bd8-b94b-b414b234bce7) king of [Zobah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000246).

locationsMap.name: Beten
locationsMap.title: Asherite town in [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080)
locationsMap.description: Beten was one of the towns on the border of Asher in [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080), though its exact site remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Bethanath
locationsMap.title: spacing variant of [Bethanath](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000030), fortified town of Naphtali
locationsMap.description: Bethanath is the spaced spelling of [Bethanath](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000030), the Naphtalite town whose Canaanite inhabitants remained among the Israelites.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Usually identified with modern Ainata or nearby sites in southern Lebanon

locationsMap.name: Bethanoth
locationsMap.title: hill-country town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Beth-anoth was a town in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119), known only from the territorial list.

locationsMap.name: Betharabah
locationsMap.title: wilderness settlement on the [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)-[Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) border near the Dead Sea
locationsMap.description: Beth-arabah was the settlement on the border of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) in the wilderness north of the Dead Sea and west of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: A site in the northwestern Dead Sea wilderness west of Jericho

locationsMap.name: Betharbel
locationsMap.title: place of devastation cited in Hosea's oracle
locationsMap.description: Beth-arbel was the place recalled in Hosea's oracle as the site of a brutal destruction; its exact identification remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Bethaven
locationsMap.title: border place east of [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032) and prophetic derisive name for Bethel
locationsMap.description: Beth-aven appears as a border place east of [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032) and also as the prophetic derisive name for Bethel, making the exact geographic reference somewhat fluid.

locationsMap.name: Bethazmaveth
locationsMap.title: postexilic Benjaminite village near [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: Beth-azmaveth was the postexilic village listed with the Benjaminite settlements near [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) and is related in name to [Azmaveth](location-id://ca49e0bd-8484-44e4-9600-ccb100919d23).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Hizma region northeast of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Bethbaalmeon
locationsMap.title: Joshua form of the Moabite town later called [Baal-meon](location-id://80dc92af-b077-4672-a9eb-a7fb7620ad83) and Beth-meon
locationsMap.description: Beth-baal-meon is the form of the eastern town in Joshua's list, corresponding to [Baal-meon](location-id://80dc92af-b077-4672-a9eb-a7fb7620ad83) and Beth-meon in related passages.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ma'in south of Madaba in Jordan

locationsMap.name: Bethbarah
locationsMap.title: [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) fords summoned by [Gideon](name-id://c639ae62-acde-4142-a3f5-fd40204fc455) against [Midian](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000152)
locationsMap.description: Beth-barah was the place or ford on the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) whose passages [Gideon](name-id://c639ae62-acde-4142-a3f5-fd40204fc455) told Ephraim to seize against the fleeing Midianites.

locationsMap.name: Bethbirei
locationsMap.title: Simeonite town in the Negev
locationsMap.description: Beth-biri was one of the Simeonite towns in the Negev and may be related in tradition to Beth-lebaoth and Beth-marcaboth.

locationsMap.name: Bethcar
locationsMap.title: place west of Mizpeh to which the Philistines were pursued
locationsMap.description: Beth-car was the point to which Israel pursued the Philistines after [Samuel](name-id://1f1722fd-38b9-474c-9c94-fcbeb1d47812)'s victory near Mizpeh.

locationsMap.name: Bethdagon
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) town of the Shephelah distinct from Beth-dagon of Asher
locationsMap.description: Beth-dagon in this record is the [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) town listed in the Shephelah; Scripture also names a distinct Beth-dagon on the border of Asher.

locationsMap.name: Bethdiblathaim
locationsMap.title: Moabite town named in Jeremiah's oracle
locationsMap.description: Beth-diblathaim was one of the Moabite towns named in Jeremiah's oracle against [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153).

locationsMap.name: Bethemek
locationsMap.title: Asherite town in western [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080)
locationsMap.description: Beth-emek was one of the towns on Asher's border in western [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080), though its exact site is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Bethezel
locationsMap.title: village in Micah's lament whose exact site is unknown
locationsMap.description: Beth-ezel appears in Micah's lament over the towns of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and is not securely identified.

locationsMap.name: Bethgamul
locationsMap.title: Moabite town named in Jeremiah's oracle
locationsMap.description: Beth-gamul was one of the Moabite towns named in Jeremiah's oracle against [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153).

locationsMap.name: Bethhaccerem
locationsMap.title: hill or settlement south of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) used as a signal point
locationsMap.description: Beth-haccherem was the district or hill south of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) used as a signal point in [Jeremiah](book-key://JER) and later named in Nehemiah's wall account.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ramat Rachel or a nearby ridge south of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Betharam
locationsMap.title: Joshua form of the Gadite town east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987)
locationsMap.description: Beth-haram is the form of the Gadite town east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) in [Joshua](book-key://JOS), corresponding to [Beth-haran](location-id://e10c14d7-9df4-4c20-aea2-c3107e64a1bc) in [Numbers](book-key://NUM) and later associated with Livias.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell er-Rameh and the area of ancient Livias in Jordan

locationsMap.name: Bethharan
locationsMap.title: [Numbers](book-key://NUM) form of the Gadite town east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987)
locationsMap.description: Beth-haran is the form in [Numbers](book-key://NUM) for the Gadite town east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) later associated with Livias, corresponding to [Beth-haram](location-id://55ed6201-774a-4bd6-9801-8c3f8018942e) in [Joshua](book-key://JOS).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell er-Rameh and the area of ancient Livias in Jordan

locationsMap.name: Bethhoglah
locationsMap.title: border settlement near the northwestern Dead Sea
locationsMap.description: Beth-hoglah was the settlement on the border of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) near [Jericho](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000116) and the northwestern shore of the Dead Sea.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ain Hajla / Qasr Hajla near Jericho in the lower Jordan Valley

locationsMap.name: Bethhoron
locationsMap.title: the twin towns of Upper and Lower Beth-horon on the ascent west of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: Beth-horon refers to the paired towns and ascent route linking the hill country with the coastal plain, a strategic corridor in multiple biblical battles.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Beit Ur al-Fauqa and Beit Ur al-Tahta in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Bethjeshimoth
locationsMap.title: plains of [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153) settlement on the northeastern Dead Sea
locationsMap.description: Beth-jeshimoth was the settlement in the plains of [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153) at the northeastern Dead Sea, named in conquest lists and later prophetic oracles.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: A site on the northeastern shore of the Dead Sea, often sought near Tell el-Azeimeh

locationsMap.name: Bethlebaoth
locationsMap.title: Simeonite town in the Negev
locationsMap.description: Beth-lebaoth was one of the Simeonite towns in the Negev and is related in the lists to other southern Simeonite settlements.

locationsMap.name: Bethmaachah
locationsMap.title: district around [Abel-beth-maachah](location-id://859e6f75-0709-4662-8bff-ce85a36afbca) in the far north
locationsMap.description: Beth-maachah was the district around [Abel-beth-maachah](location-id://859e6f75-0709-4662-8bff-ce85a36afbca) in the far north, the region through which [Sheba](name-id://87da963f-c366-46e3-b16c-038dc798b0e5)'s rebellion passed.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The district around Tell Abelbethmaachah near the Israel-Lebanon border

locationsMap.name: Bethmarcaboth
locationsMap.title: Simeonite town in the Negev
locationsMap.description: Beth-marcaboth was one of the Simeonite towns in the Negev and appears in both Joshua and Chronicles.

locationsMap.name: Bethmeon
locationsMap.title: Jeremiah form of the town also called [Baal-meon](location-id://80dc92af-b077-4672-a9eb-a7fb7620ad83)
locationsMap.description: Beth-meon is Jeremiah's form of the Transjordanian town also called [Baal-meon](location-id://80dc92af-b077-4672-a9eb-a7fb7620ad83) and [Beth-baal-meon](location-id://c81ca0fa-f65d-433e-8fe1-a4af860631dc).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ma'in south of Madaba in Jordan

locationsMap.name: Bethnimrah
locationsMap.title: Gadite town east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) later known as Nimrin
locationsMap.description: Beth-nimrah was the Gadite town east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) that later tradition preserves in the name Nimrin.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell Nimrin in Jordan east of the lower Jordan Valley

locationsMap.name: Bethpazzez
locationsMap.title: Issacharite town named in the tribal allotment
locationsMap.description: Beth-pazzez was one of the towns in Issachar's territorial list, though its exact site is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Bethpalet
locationsMap.title: southern town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) later resettled after exile
locationsMap.description: Beth-pelet was a southern [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) town in the Negev and appears again among the settlements of the postexilic community.

locationsMap.name: Bethpeor
locationsMap.title: settlement opposite [Peor](location-id://479a8bc3-a004-4961-b621-109fa14b0b7d) near the plains of [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153)
locationsMap.description: Beth-peor was the settlement opposite [Peor](location-id://479a8bc3-a004-4961-b621-109fa14b0b7d) in the plains of [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153), associated with Israel's camp and the region of [Moses](name-id://fff825ad-31e8-4843-a7dc-cd82e9878d73)'s burial.

locationsMap.name: Bethrehob
locationsMap.title: spacing variant of [Bethrehob](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000035), northern town or district
locationsMap.description: Bethrehob is the spaced spelling of [Bethrehob](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000035), the northern district or settlement near [Dan](location-id://dadc79b1-e84f-40e0-ab31-2fa96b6ed4bd) and Lebo-hamath.

locationsMap.name: Bethshan
locationsMap.title: Samuel form of [Beth-shean](location-id://c6ddfad2-cdfa-4992-9bb8-479e7c6bc9ca) at the junction of [Jezreel](location-id://01fb54a8-39da-4de4-9ba9-6c91d7efff5b) and [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) valleys
locationsMap.description: Beth-shan is the form used in Samuel for the strategic city where the [Philistines](name-id://35245676-ecab-4457-84b4-cc81d8d63bff) fastened [Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb)'s body after [Gilboa](location-id://54a1ec6e-0295-4eb7-a2ca-6195a3854212).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Beth-Shean in modern Beit She'an, Israel

locationsMap.name: Bethshean
locationsMap.title: [Joshua](book-key://JOS) and [Judges](book-key://JDG) form of the strategic city later called [Beth-shan](location-id://7b0f49d3-4da0-488e-ac64-672963954344)
locationsMap.description: Beth-shean is the form used in the tribal and royal lists for the strategic city at the junction of the [Jezreel](location-id://01fb54a8-39da-4de4-9ba9-6c91d7efff5b) and [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) valleys.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Beth-Shean in modern Beit She'an, Israel

locationsMap.name: Bethshittah
locationsMap.title: settlement on the line of Midian's flight after [Gideon](name-id://c639ae62-acde-4142-a3f5-fd40204fc455)'s victory
locationsMap.description: Beth-shittah was the place toward which the Midianites fled after [Gideon](name-id://c639ae62-acde-4142-a3f5-fd40204fc455)'s victory, named on the route toward [Zererath](location-id://722228f6-8f93-4fe6-8885-55ef09491ee8) and [Abel-meholah](location-id://d655b227-bc54-4c54-a3d9-a78f621a925d); it is often connected with the Shutta or Beit HaShita area in the [Jezreel](location-id://01fb54a8-39da-4de4-9ba9-6c91d7efff5b) Valley.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Often identified with the Shutta or Beit HaShita area in the Jezreel Valley of Israel

locationsMap.name: Bethtappuah
locationsMap.title: hill-country town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) near [Hebron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000103)
locationsMap.description: Beth-tappuah was a town in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and is commonly identified with modern Taffuh west of [Hebron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000103).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Taffuh west of Hebron in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Bethzur
locationsMap.title: fortified [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) town north of [Hebron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000103)
locationsMap.description: Bethzur was a fortified town in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and later gave its name to a district in the time of [Nehemiah](name-id://46c4c07f-dde8-4466-a278-6e40a8d3e7f1); it is securely associated with Khirbet Beit Sur.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Khirbet Beit Sur north of Hebron in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Bethesda
locationsMap.title: pool in [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) by the sheep gate where [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) healed the infirm man
locationsMap.description: Bethesda was the pool in [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) by the sheep gate where [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) healed the man who had long been infirm; the site is identified with the Pool of Bethesda near St Anne's Church.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Pool of Bethesda near St Anne's Church in Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Bethphage
locationsMap.title: village on the [Mount of Olives](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000158) near [Bethany](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000031) and [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: Bethphage was the village on or near the [Mount of Olives](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000158) named with [Bethany](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000031) in the triumphal-entry narratives; its exact ancient site is uncertain, though the traditional location lies near the southeastern slope of the mount.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Traditional site on the southeastern Mount of Olives near modern al-Tur and al-Eizariya

locationsMap.name: Bethuel
locationsMap.title: Simeonite town in the south, probably the same place as [Bethul](location-id://a9cc4fd4-965a-49ba-b0c9-ece055afd3e4) and [Chesil](location-id://e67bf0d0-b2f1-4cb8-a8b3-096e02455776)
locationsMap.description: Bethuel was one of the southern towns of [Simeon](name-id://8023a792-fa1b-4465-89b5-09f437ac5081) in Chronicles and is commonly taken as the same place as [Bethul](location-id://a9cc4fd4-965a-49ba-b0c9-ece055afd3e4) in [Joshua](book-key://JOS) and [Chesil](location-id://e67bf0d0-b2f1-4cb8-a8b3-096e02455776) in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)'s town list.

locationsMap.name: Bethul
locationsMap.title: Simeonite town in the south, probably identical with [Bethuel](location-id://75c29887-74ea-40bc-a8c2-3f77f49864fb) and [Chesil](location-id://e67bf0d0-b2f1-4cb8-a8b3-096e02455776)
locationsMap.description: Bethul was one of the towns assigned to [Simeon](name-id://8023a792-fa1b-4465-89b5-09f437ac5081) in [Joshua](book-key://JOS) and is commonly identified with [Bethuel](location-id://75c29887-74ea-40bc-a8c2-3f77f49864fb) in Chronicles and [Chesil](location-id://e67bf0d0-b2f1-4cb8-a8b3-096e02455776) in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)'s list.

locationsMap.name: Betonim
locationsMap.title: Gadite border town east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987)
locationsMap.description: Betonim was a town on the border of [Gad](name-id://0b987f5d-4e64-4b73-a3e2-7f6b47dd7f46) in Transjordan, named in the description of the tribal allotment; its exact site is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Beyond the River
locationsMap.title: Persian imperial territory west of the [Euphrates](location-id://0bdad9de-f6dc-4681-8a5a-54526382bc9f)
locationsMap.description: Beyond the River is the administrative name for Transeuphrates, the Persian imperial territory west of the [Euphrates](location-id://0bdad9de-f6dc-4681-8a5a-54526382bc9f) that included [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and neighboring lands.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Persian satrapy of Transeuphrates west of the Euphrates

locationsMap.name: Bezek
locationsMap.title: Canaanite town where [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and [Simeon](name-id://8023a792-fa1b-4465-89b5-09f437ac5081) defeated [Adonibezek](name-id://aa335aee-409d-4e55-a7d1-439ae4b99183)
locationsMap.description: This Bezek is the town where [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and [Simeon](name-id://8023a792-fa1b-4465-89b5-09f437ac5081) defeated the Canaanites and captured [Adonibezek](name-id://aa335aee-409d-4e55-a7d1-439ae4b99183); its exact site is uncertain and it may not be the same Bezek where [Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb) later numbered [Israel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000108).

locationsMap.name: Bezer
locationsMap.title: Reubenite city of refuge on the wilderness tableland
locationsMap.description: Bezer was the city of refuge in the wilderness on the tableland allotted to [Reuben](name-id://82279de3-ec8f-482d-a58d-119054ecb790) and later given to the Levites; its exact archaeological site remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Bileam
locationsMap.title: Manassite Levitical town usually identified with [Ibleam](location-id://78607a80-3155-437a-aeeb-70f7f1ca66fe)
locationsMap.description: Bileam was the Manassite town given to the Kohathite Levites in Chronicles and is commonly understood as another form of [Ibleam](location-id://78607a80-3155-437a-aeeb-70f7f1ca66fe).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Usually identified with Khirbet Bil'ameh south of Jenin in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Bilhah
locationsMap.title: Simeonite town in the south, probably the same place as [Balah](location-id://bd91ef20-e0bc-4f53-b96a-a27d5ce4b33e)
locationsMap.description: Bilhah was a southern Simeonite town listed in Chronicles and is commonly taken as the same place as [Balah](location-id://bd91ef20-e0bc-4f53-b96a-a27d5ce4b33e) in Joshua's tribal list.

locationsMap.name: Bithynia
locationsMap.title: Roman province in northwestern Asia Minor
locationsMap.description: Bithynia was the Roman province in northwestern Asia Minor that [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) was prevented from entering and whose believers [Peter](name-id://2bcada1c-b00a-4214-8a2d-5a7b991f6641) later addressed.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Northwestern Turkey along the Black Sea and Sea of Marmara

locationsMap.name: Bozez
locationsMap.title: northern crag opposite [Seneh](location-id://f221959a-dd45-414d-9e71-83ce25dbcb0e) near [Michmash](location-id://ee19b0f3-9647-4ed1-9f48-d9bef91d04fd)
locationsMap.description: Bozez was one of the two rocky crags in the pass between [Michmash](location-id://ee19b0f3-9647-4ed1-9f48-d9bef91d04fd) and [Geba](location-id://b070825c-868d-4992-a20c-b187b9380c70) that frame [Jonathan](name-id://0654ad89-fc99-484a-8771-b277e9225953)'s attack on the Philistine outpost.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: A crag above Wadi Suweinit between Michmash and Geba in the central Benjamin plateau

locationsMap.name: Bozkath
locationsMap.title: Judahite town of the Shephelah
locationsMap.description: Bozkath was a town in the Shephelah of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and is especially remembered as the home of Adaiah, mother of King [Josiah](name-id://60cb7338-d759-439a-8ad6-ecccf0f9d30a).

locationsMap.name: Bozrah
locationsMap.title: principal city of [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064), home of an Edomite king and target of prophetic judgment
locationsMap.description: Bozrah was one of the chief cities of [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064), associated with [Jobab](name-id://f299754a-49bf-4626-a47f-cd6835ed865e) king of Edom and later with prophetic oracles against Edom; it is usually identified with Busaira in southern Jordan.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Busaira in southern Jordan

locationsMap.name: Broad Wall
locationsMap.title: broad section of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)'s fortifications repaired in [Nehemiah](book-key://NEH)
locationsMap.description: The Broad Wall was the broad stretch of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)'s fortification named in [Nehemiah](book-key://NEH) and known archaeologically from remains in the Jewish Quarter.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Broad Wall remains in the Jewish Quarter of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Brook of the Willows
locationsMap.title: stream in [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153) named in Isaiah's oracle
locationsMap.description: The Brook of the Willows was the stream named in Isaiah's oracle against [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153), where refugees carry away their wealth; its exact identification is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Buz
locationsMap.title: Arabian land or district named with [Dedan](location-id://ed08e1a2-e6c2-4ed4-9609-603535fd949c) and [Tema](location-id://29940054-8485-454c-ab6a-319928e75966)
locationsMap.description: Buz was the Arabian land or district named with [Dedan](location-id://ed08e1a2-e6c2-4ed4-9609-603535fd949c) and [Tema](location-id://29940054-8485-454c-ab6a-319928e75966) in Jeremiah's oracle against the nations, probably corresponding to a tribal territory in the northern Arabian desert.

locationsMap.name: Benjamin
locationsMap.title: smallest tribal territory bordering [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and [Ephraim](name-id://4ad1140c-2b95-4513-bd55-ed594805df5f)
locationsMap.description: Benjamin was the tribal territory allotted to the descendants of [Jacob](name-id://23ed64d8-8458-49af-9b51-f578ab3262d9)'s son Benjamin, lying between [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and [Ephraim](name-id://4ad1140c-2b95-4513-bd55-ed594805df5f) and including the approaches to [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117), [Gibeon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000088), [Mizpah](location-id://4c916b4d-a2ed-47ac-853b-e512b1fb7068), and [Ramah](location-id://87bccdaa-b5c2-455b-8672-eec8740c0007).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: central highlands north of Jerusalem in modern Israel and the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Bethzur
locationsMap.title: fortified Judean hill town south of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: Bethzur was a Judahite town fortified by [Rehoboam](name-id://68d5eac0-52b9-4b0b-b484-8c7b5c3b8971) and later ruled over in part by [Nehemiah](name-id://46c4c07f-dde8-4466-a278-6e40a8d3e7f1)'s day; [Nehemiah](name-id://7d660af0-8058-4ea7-9317-a9c3fd16a824) son of [Azbuk](name-id://6a14089b-72e5-474e-bbfe-9830aa40a682) was ruler of half its district.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Khirbet et-Tubeiqa, south of Bethlehem

locationsMap.name: Cabul
locationsMap.title: settlement in [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080) associated with Asher and [Solomon](name-id://509b7c2f-b8bf-4a4d-a393-550a7a4b259f)'s gift to [Hiram](name-id://26687f64-c119-4c2a-a165-293c934a08f1)
locationsMap.description: Cabul was a settlement in the [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080) on Asher's border and later the name of the district or cluster of towns that [Solomon](name-id://509b7c2f-b8bf-4a4d-a393-550a7a4b259f) gave to [Hiram](name-id://26687f64-c119-4c2a-a165-293c934a08f1) king of [Tyre](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000226); it is commonly identified with modern Kabul east of Acre.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Kabul in the Galilee of northern Israel

locationsMap.name: Calneh
locationsMap.title: disputed biblical city-name in [Shinar](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000204) and northern Syria traditions
locationsMap.description: Calneh is named in [Genesis 10:10](verse-key://GEN 10:10) among [Nimrod](name-id://80b191de-d8ed-486d-bbb5-bd36756496ac)'s cities in [Shinar](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000204) and in [Amos 6:2](verse-key://AMO 6:2) beside [Hamath](location-id://e88700f4-7b74-49f1-bf22-d4a4a6992b62) and [Gath](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000082); the [Genesis](book-key://GEN) reading may preserve a corrupt expression rather than a recoverable city, while the Amos place is commonly associated with [Calno](location-id://55c8ce25-9381-411f-9c8c-643cf84c5be0) or Kullani in northern Syria.

locationsMap.name: Cana
locationsMap.title: Galilean village associated with [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab)' first sign at a wedding feast
locationsMap.description: Cana of [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080) is the village named in John's Gospel as the site of [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab)' first sign, the turning of water into wine, and of the healing of the royal official's son; its precise location remains disputed, with Khirbet Qana and Kafr Kanna the leading candidates.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Disputed; commonly identified either with Khirbet Qana in lower Galilee or with Kafr Kanna northeast of Nazareth in Israel

locationsMap.name: Canaan
locationsMap.title: territory of the southern Levant promised to [Abraham](name-id://4ce14dfc-b652-45d9-ac05-5f0cf716c412) and later inherited by Israel
locationsMap.description: Canaan is the biblical land of the southern Levant promised to [Abraham](name-id://4ce14dfc-b652-45d9-ac05-5f0cf716c412) and his descendants; in Scripture it denotes the territory later occupied by Israel and neighboring peoples between the patriarchal age and the conquest.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The southern Levant, especially modern Israel, the Palestinian territories, Lebanon, and parts of Jordan and southwestern Syria

locationsMap.name: Capernaum
locationsMap.title: Galilean town that became the center of [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab)' public ministry
locationsMap.description: Capernaum was a fishing town on the northwestern shore of the [Sea of Galilee](location-id://44329b87-3c5b-4d27-9fcf-e386f2aebc5b) and became the main center of [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab)' ministry in [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080); the site is identified with Tell Hum.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell Hum on the northwestern shore of the Sea of Galilee in Israel

locationsMap.name: Cappadocia
locationsMap.title: inland Anatolian region represented at Pentecost and addressed in [1 Peter](book-key://1PE)
locationsMap.description: Cappadocia was the inland region of central Anatolia whose Jewish pilgrims were present at Pentecost and whose believers were among the recipients of [1 Peter](book-key://1PE).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Historical region of central Anatolia in modern Turkey, especially around Nevsehir, Kayseri, Aksaray, and Nigde

locationsMap.name: Carchemish
locationsMap.title: fortified [Euphrates](location-id://0bdad9de-f6dc-4681-8a5a-54526382bc9f) city on the Syria-Anatolia frontier
locationsMap.description: Carchemish was a major fortified city on the [Euphrates](location-id://0bdad9de-f6dc-4681-8a5a-54526382bc9f) controlling a key crossing between northern Syria and Anatolia; it appears in Scripture in connection with [Assyria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000023), [Egypt](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000065), and [Babylon](location-id://8939f721-e16f-4837-84f0-ec3dcc65ea70).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The ruins of Karkamis on the Turkey-Syria border by the Euphrates

locationsMap.name: Cenchrea
locationsMap.title: KJV form of Cenchreae, [Corinth](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000058)'s eastern harbor
locationsMap.description: Cenchrea is the King James spelling of the eastern port of [Corinth](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000058) on the Saronic Gulf, known in Greek and modern scholarship as Cenchreae; [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) sailed from there and Phoebe served the church there.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Kechries east of ancient Corinth in Greece

locationsMap.name: Chaldea
locationsMap.title: southern Mesopotamian territory associated with the Chaldeans and Babylonian rule
locationsMap.description: Chaldea was the low, marshy territory of southern [Mesopotamia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000151) associated with the Chaldean tribes and later with Neo-Babylonian power; in the Hebrew Bible the term can also extend more broadly to [Babylonia](location-id://a4fdc004-f375-4bf2-a0ad-8d77ec7fce98).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The southern Mesopotamian lowlands of Iraq around the lower Tigris and Euphrates near the head of the Persian Gulf

locationsMap.name: Chorazin
locationsMap.title: Galilean town condemned alongside [Capernaum](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000046) in the Gospels
locationsMap.description: Chorazin was a town on the Korazim Plateau north of the [Sea of Galilee](location-id://44329b87-3c5b-4d27-9fcf-e386f2aebc5b), remembered in the Gospels as one of the places reproved by [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) for unbelief; it is identified with Khirbet Kerazeh.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Khirbet Kerazeh or Korazim north of the Sea of Galilee in Israel

locationsMap.name: Cilicia
locationsMap.title: southeastern Asia Minor region linked with [Tarsus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000218) and early Christian travel
locationsMap.description: Cilicia was the southeastern Anatolian region around [Tarsus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000218) and the Cilician plain, repeatedly mentioned in [Acts](book-key://ACT) and [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s letters as a place of diaspora Jews, Roman administration, and missionary travel.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The coastal and inland region around Adana, Mersin, and neighboring parts of southern Turkey

locationsMap.name: Crete
locationsMap.title: large Mediterranean island visited on [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s voyage and assigned to [Titus](name-id://edebc9dd-3078-4022-b294-4ecd27682d47)
locationsMap.description: Crete was the large island south of the Aegean mainland skirted during [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s stormy voyage to [Rome](location-id://ff427d76-a9e7-4a50-bc2d-61b6b459e87b); [Titus](name-id://edebc9dd-3078-4022-b294-4ecd27682d47) was later left there to set the churches in order.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Greek island of Crete

locationsMap.name: Corinth
locationsMap.title: Achaian city where [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) founded a major church
locationsMap.description: Corinth was the chief city of Roman [Achaia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002) on the isthmus linking mainland [Greece](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000094) and the Peloponnese; [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) lived and worked there and wrote letters to its church.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ancient Corinth near modern Korinthos in Greece

locationsMap.name: Cush
locationsMap.title: land south of [Egypt](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000065) usually identified with Nubia and the kingdom of Kush
locationsMap.description: Cush is the biblical land south of [Egypt](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000065) identified chiefly with Nubia and the kingdom of Kush in the Middle Nile region; some early passages have been interpreted more broadly, but the name normally denotes the Upper Nile lands of modern Sudan and southern Egypt.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Nubia and the kingdom of Kush in modern Sudan and southern Egypt

locationsMap.name: Cyprus
locationsMap.title: eastern Mediterranean island tied to [Barnabas](name-id://ba3667d2-9c64-4e6e-8836-beb53828cb13) and [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s first mission
locationsMap.description: Cyprus was the large eastern Mediterranean island associated with [Barnabas](name-id://ba3667d2-9c64-4e6e-8836-beb53828cb13) and with the opening stage of [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s first missionary journey; it also appears in prophetic and trade texts of the Old Testament.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The island of Cyprus in the eastern Mediterranean

locationsMap.name: Cabbon
locationsMap.title: Shephelah town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) near [Eglon](location-id://42127334-9744-4a9d-8017-d33806005272) with unidentified site
locationsMap.description: Cabbon was a town in the Shephelah of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) named near [Eglon](location-id://42127334-9744-4a9d-8017-d33806005272) in Joshua's list; its site is unknown, though some have compared it with Machbena.

locationsMap.name: Caesarea
locationsMap.title: Herodian port city and Roman administrative center of Judaea
locationsMap.description: Caesarea was Herod the Great's harbor city on the Mediterranean and the Roman administrative capital of Judaea; [Cornelius](name-id://6df0b109-cfff-41ab-930d-9cc40bca494c) lived there, [Peter](name-id://2bcada1c-b00a-4214-8a2d-5a7b991f6641) visited it, Philip settled there, and [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) was repeatedly held there.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Caesarea Maritima National Park on the Mediterranean coast of Israel

locationsMap.name: Caesarea Philippi
locationsMap.title: city at the foot of [Hermon](location-id://9ed57141-d70e-475b-b75f-a72a0f541a48) where [Peter](name-id://2bcada1c-b00a-4214-8a2d-5a7b991f6641) confessed [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) as the Christ
locationsMap.description: Caesarea Philippi was the city near the springs of Banias at the foot of [Mount Hermon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000156) where [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) asked his disciples who he was and [Peter](name-id://2bcada1c-b00a-4214-8a2d-5a7b991f6641) confessed him as the Christ.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Banias at the foot of Mount Hermon in the Golan Heights

locationsMap.name: Calah
locationsMap.title: Assyrian city built by [Nimrod](name-id://80b191de-d8ed-486d-bbb5-bd36756496ac) and identified with ancient Kalhu
locationsMap.description: Calah was one of the chief Assyrian cities in [Genesis](book-key://GEN) and is identified with ancient Kalhu, the site later called Nimrud, south of Mosul on the Tigris.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Nimrud south of Mosul in Iraq

locationsMap.name: Calno
locationsMap.title: KJV form of [Calneh](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000043) or Kullani in Isaiah's oracle against [Assyria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000023)
locationsMap.description: Calno is the KJV place-name in [Isaiah 10:9](verse-key://ISA 10:9), paired with [Carchemish](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000048), [Hamath](location-id://e88700f4-7b74-49f1-bf22-d4a4a6992b62), [Arpad](location-id://d7b0d901-69c5-4e01-aa01-b20679e872eb), [Samaria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000196), and [Damascus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000061) as conquered cities; it is commonly associated with the [Calneh](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000043) of [Amos 6:2](verse-key://AMO 6:2) and with Kullani or Kullan-Koy near Arpad in northern Syria, though the exact identification remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Canneh
locationsMap.title: trading locality named among [Tyre](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000226)'s merchants in [Ezekiel](book-key://EZK)
locationsMap.description: Canneh is named in [Ezekiel 27:23](verse-key://EZK 27:23) among the merchants trading with [Tyre](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000226), alongside [Haran](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000097), Eden, [Sheba](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000200), Asshur, and [Chilmad](location-id://05ee5379-5066-4a28-b3f9-153749b6c58b); it has been associated with [Calneh](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000043) or with Xenophon's Kainai near the Tigris, but the identification is not secure.

locationsMap.name: Caphtor
locationsMap.title: ancestral homeland of the Caphtorim and the Philistine migrations
locationsMap.description: Caphtor is the land from which the Caphtorim and later the Philistines were said to come; scholars often connect it with [Crete](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000055) or another eastern Mediterranean coastland, but no single identification is certain.

locationsMap.name: Carmel
locationsMap.title: mountain ridge by the [Great Sea](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000093) associated with [Elijah](name-id://f8f9a290-0e18-4c0f-8f4c-bb8201e8c652) and biblical poetry
locationsMap.description: Carmel is the prominent mountain ridge by the [Great Sea](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000093) associated with [Elijah](name-id://f8f9a290-0e18-4c0f-8f4c-bb8201e8c652)'s contest against the prophets of Baal and with the fertile heights praised in biblical poetry.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Mount Carmel ridge in northern Israel

locationsMap.name: Casiphia
locationsMap.title: Babylonian locality on the [Ahava](location-id://50f65d00-8d29-43b0-91b2-87ec8900ba03) route where [Ezra](name-id://1608b225-d488-4910-a6d6-5ac8db7c90cd) sought Levites
locationsMap.description: Casiphia was the place in [Babylonia](location-id://a4fdc004-f375-4bf2-a0ad-8d77ec7fce98) to which [Ezra](name-id://1608b225-d488-4910-a6d6-5ac8db7c90cd) sent for ministers for the house of God before the return to [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117); its exact site is unknown, though the name was later associated with silver or a treasury.

locationsMap.name: Chebar
locationsMap.title: Babylonian canal where [Ezekiel](name-id://064f216a-deee-458d-9e0c-7e8ec7f38946) saw his inaugural visions
locationsMap.description: Chebar was the great canal near Nippur in [Babylonia](location-id://a4fdc004-f375-4bf2-a0ad-8d77ec7fce98) where the Judean exiles lived and where [Ezekiel](name-id://064f216a-deee-458d-9e0c-7e8ec7f38946) received the visions that open and shape his book.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Kebar Canal near Nippur in Iraq

locationsMap.name: Chepharhaammonai
locationsMap.title: Benjaminite town possibly identical with Kefr Ana near [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032)
locationsMap.description: Chepharhaammonai was a town in [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) and has been tentatively identified with Kefr Ana, a ruined site northeast of [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032).

locationsMap.name: Chephirah
locationsMap.title: Gibeonite town allotted to [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) and resettled after the exile
locationsMap.description: Chephirah was one of the Gibeonite towns named in [Joshua](book-key://JOS) and later listed among [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef)'s settlements; it is identified with Khirbet el-Kafira northwest of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Khirbet el-Kafira northwest of Jerusalem in the Benjamin hill country

locationsMap.name: Cherith
locationsMap.title: seasonal brook where [Elijah](name-id://f8f9a290-0e18-4c0f-8f4c-bb8201e8c652) was hidden during the drought
locationsMap.description: Cherith was the seasonal brook or wadi where [Elijah](name-id://f8f9a290-0e18-4c0f-8f4c-bb8201e8c652) was hidden and fed by ravens after announcing the drought; it is usually identified with Wadi al-Yabis east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987), though other wadis have been proposed.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Usually identified with Wadi al-Yabis east of the Jordan in modern Jordan

locationsMap.name: Cherub
locationsMap.title: Babylonian locality from which undocumented families returned
locationsMap.description: Cherub was a place in [Babylonia](location-id://a4fdc004-f375-4bf2-a0ad-8d77ec7fce98) from which families of uncertain genealogy returned with [Zerubbabel](name-id://0d7601da-e748-429c-96ec-359cc4dd88ba) after the exile; its site is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Chesalon
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) border town identified with Kasla west of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: Chesalon was a landmark on the northern boundary of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and is generally identified with Kasla or Kesla on the ridge west of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117), a site that preserves the ancient name.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Kasla or Kesla west of Jerusalem in the Judaean hill country

locationsMap.name: Chesil
locationsMap.title: southern [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) town probably identical with Bethul and Bethuel
locationsMap.description: Chesil was a town in the far south of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and is commonly taken to be the same settlement that appears elsewhere as [Bethul](location-id://a9cc4fd4-965a-49ba-b0c9-ece055afd3e4) and [Bethuel](location-id://75c29887-74ea-40bc-a8c2-3f77f49864fb); the equivalence is likely, but the precise site remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Chesulloth
locationsMap.title: town near [Mount Tabor](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000160) usually equated with Chislothtabor
locationsMap.description: Chesulloth was a town named in the tribal lists near [Mount Tabor](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000160) and is commonly identified with [Chislothtabor](location-id://b5af26bb-7849-4865-942d-2910c51f5717), represented by modern Iksal.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Iksal southeast of Nazareth in Israel

locationsMap.name: Chezib
locationsMap.title: variant name for [Achzib](location-id://e5e9c33d-ae22-45e9-ba4b-06feba9c92ad) of Judah, a Shephelah town linked to [Shelah](name-id://059a069e-7b99-4bbe-8062-94e62e46f632)'s birth
locationsMap.description: Chezib is the name used in [Genesis](book-key://GEN) for the Judah town also called [Achzib](location-id://e5e9c33d-ae22-45e9-ba4b-06feba9c92ad) of Judah; it was associated with the birth of [Shelah](name-id://059a069e-7b99-4bbe-8062-94e62e46f632) and is usually sought near [Adullam](location-id://9115a436-027f-4c32-b221-735767cd01c6) in the Elah Valley region, though the exact site remains debated.

locationsMap.name: Chilmad
locationsMap.title: trading locality or district in Ezekiel's lament over [Tyre](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000226) with disputed reading
locationsMap.description: Chilmad is named in [Ezekiel 27:23](verse-key://EZK 27:23) among [Tyre](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000226)'s trading partners, but the word may preserve a place-name, a district-name, or a corrupt textual reading; proposed identifications such as Kalwadha near Baghdad remain doubtful.

locationsMap.name: Chinnereth
locationsMap.title: fortified Naphtalite town that gave its name to the [Sea of Galilee](location-id://44329b87-3c5b-4d27-9fcf-e386f2aebc5b)
locationsMap.description: Chinnereth was a fortified town in Naphtali on the northwestern shore of the [Sea of Galilee](location-id://44329b87-3c5b-4d27-9fcf-e386f2aebc5b), and its name was later applied to the lake itself; the site is identified with Tel Kinrot or Tell el-'Oreimeh.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Kinrot or Tell el-'Oreimeh on the northwestern shore of the Sea of Galilee in Israel

locationsMap.name: Chinneroth
locationsMap.title: lakeside district around Kinneret and the [Sea of Galilee](location-id://44329b87-3c5b-4d27-9fcf-e386f2aebc5b)
locationsMap.description: Chinneroth is the plural form used in [Joshua](book-key://JOS) and Kings for the district around Kinneret and, in some contexts, for the lake later known as the [Sea of Galilee](location-id://44329b87-3c5b-4d27-9fcf-e386f2aebc5b); the name derives from the town of Kinneret or Tel Kinrot on the lake's northwestern shore.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Kinneret or Gennesaret region around the northwestern Sea of Galilee in Israel

locationsMap.name: Chios
locationsMap.title: Aegean island passed on [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s return voyage to [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: Chios was the Aegean island off the coast of Asia Minor where [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s ship came the day after leaving [Mitylene](location-id://8e1f05e8-1e59-4220-9928-5c54ff6477c2) on the journey recorded in [Acts 20](chapter-key://ACT 20).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Greek island of Chios off the coast of western Turkey

locationsMap.name: Chislothtabor
locationsMap.title: border town on Zebulun's frontier near [Mount Tabor](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000160)
locationsMap.description: Chislothtabor was the border point on Zebulun's frontier near [Mount Tabor](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000160), commonly identified with Iksal southeast of [Nazareth](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000167).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Iksal southeast of Nazareth in Israel

locationsMap.name: City of Destruction
locationsMap.title: textual reading in [Isaiah](book-key://ISA) for the Egyptian city of Heliopolis or [On](location-id://fb1b6881-b170-444a-98f2-ac80a135e65f)
locationsMap.description: City of Destruction is the alternate Hebrew reading in [Isaiah 19:18](verse-key://ISA 19:18) for the Egyptian city more commonly understood as the City of the Sun, that is Heliopolis or biblical [On](location-id://fb1b6881-b170-444a-98f2-ac80a135e65f); the underlying place is the same, but the reading itself is textually disputed.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ancient Heliopolis or On, now in the El-Matareya and Ain Shams area of Cairo, Egypt

locationsMap.name: City of Salt
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) wilderness town near [Engedi](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000070) with very uncertain site
locationsMap.description: City of Salt was one of the six cities in the wilderness of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) named near [Nibshan](location-id://b1da2bba-59be-4cd7-890e-3befcc56d6a5) and [En-gedi](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000070); its site is very uncertain, though Tell el-Milh has sometimes been proposed.

locationsMap.name: Cnidus
locationsMap.title: Carian harbor city reached by [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s storm-driven ship
locationsMap.description: Cnidus was the harbor city at the tip of the Datca peninsula in Caria where [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s ship came before adverse winds forced it south toward [Crete](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000055); the site is now known as Knidos.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Knidos on Cape Krio at the end of the Datca peninsula in Turkey

locationsMap.name: Corner Gate
locationsMap.title: [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) gate on the northwestern reach of the city wall
locationsMap.description: The Corner Gate was a gate on [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)'s wall mentioned with the Ephraim Gate, the Valley Gate, and the Tower of Hananeel; it appears to have stood near the northwestern angle of the city, though its exact site is uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: A gate near the northwestern angle of ancient Jerusalem, exact location uncertain

locationsMap.name: Coos
locationsMap.title: Aegean island called Coos in the KJV and visited on [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s voyage
locationsMap.description: Cos, called Coos in the King James Version, was the island where [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s party arrived after leaving [Miletus](location-id://2a3d81b9-2d80-47f4-ac15-1aae05193c1a) on the voyage toward [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Greek island of Kos in the southeastern Aegean

locationsMap.name: Chun
locationsMap.title: Chronicles form of the Aramean city also called [Berothai](location-id://e7ead3d6-fa5b-4940-bf66-9cb98999f550)
locationsMap.description: Cun, called Chun in the King James Version, is the Chronicles name for the Aramean city from which [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) took much bronze from [Hadadezer](name-id://2d9ff281-73b3-4bd8-b94b-b414b234bce7); it is commonly taken to be the same place as [Berothai](location-id://e7ead3d6-fa5b-4940-bf66-9cb98999f550) and related to [Berothah](location-id://60a10e55-d5f7-4b73-bebf-74d560784ee5).

locationsMap.name: Cushan
locationsMap.title: poetic name for [Cush](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000059) paired with [Midian](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000152) in [Habakkuk](book-key://HAB)
locationsMap.description: Cushan in Habakkuk's theophany is generally understood as a poetic or extended form of [Cush](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000059) rather than a separate well-defined country; it is set in parallel with the land of [Midian](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000152).

locationsMap.name: Cuth
locationsMap.title: short form of [Cuthah](location-id://97d8e66f-512c-4b37-bef9-dd074b699ab5), the Mesopotamian city linked with settlers in [Samaria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000196)
locationsMap.description: Cuth is the shorter biblical form of [Cuthah](location-id://97d8e66f-512c-4b37-bef9-dd074b699ab5), the Mesopotamian city identified with Kutha or Tell Ibrahim in Iraq, from which settlers were brought into [Samaria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000196) after the Assyrian deportations.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell Ibrahim, ancient Kutha, in Babil Governorate, Iraq

locationsMap.name: Cuthah
locationsMap.title: Mesopotamian city linked with settlers transplanted into [Samaria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000196)
locationsMap.description: Cuthah was the Mesopotamian city identified with Kutha or Tell Ibrahim in Iraq, from which settlers were brought into [Samaria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000196) after the Assyrian deportations.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell Ibrahim, ancient Kutha, in Babil Governorate, Iraq

locationsMap.name: Cyrene
locationsMap.title: major city of Cyrenaica whose people appear repeatedly in the New Testament
locationsMap.description: Cyrene was the chief city of Cyrenaica in North Africa; Simon of Cyrene carried [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab)' cross, pilgrims from Cyrene were at Pentecost, and men of [Cyprus](location-id://cddb5c4a-d659-447d-b7bd-cd2aee99dde2) and Cyrene helped spread the gospel at [Antioch](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000012).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The archaeological site of Cyrene near Shahhat in Libya

locationsMap.name: Country of the Gadarenes
locationsMap.title: district east of the [sea of Galilee](location-id://44329b87-3c5b-4d27-9fcf-e386f2aebc5b) where [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) healed the demoniac
locationsMap.description: The country of the Gadarenes is the KJV name for the district on the eastern side of the lake, over against [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080), where [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) came over unto the other side of the sea and met the man with the unclean spirit who dwelt among the tombs and answered that his name was Legion, after which the devils entered a great herd of swine and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea and were choked ([Mark 5:1-13](verse-key://MRK 5:1-13)). The whole multitude of the district then besought him to depart from them ([Luke 8:37](verse-key://LUK 8:37)). The name is taken from Gadara, a city of the [Decapolis](location-id://17b83fd0-81f4-4a65-a0ee-51549aa8b039) some ten kilometres southeast of the lake at modern Umm Qais in Jordan, but the parallel gospel texts and manuscripts also read Gerasenes and Gergesenes, and the precise stretch of shore where the miracle took place remains disputed, with Kursi on the eastern shore identified by Origen and Eusebius as Gergesa.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: District east of the Sea of Galilee associated with Gadara, modern Umm Qais in Jordan

locationsMap.name: Chorashan
locationsMap.title: place in [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)'s spoil list, probably the same southern town as [Ashan](location-id://a996092a-1f04-4e3f-a1e4-a867de330047)
locationsMap.description: Bor-ashan appears in [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)'s spoil list and is commonly understood as the same southern town otherwise called [Ashan](location-id://a996092a-1f04-4e3f-a1e4-a867de330047).

locationsMap.name: Damascus
locationsMap.title: ancient city of [Syria](location-id://f4fe75e3-4f92-4642-bf57-3d6a59931322) associated with [Aram](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000015) and [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s conversion
locationsMap.description: Damascus is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities of [Syria](location-id://f4fe75e3-4f92-4642-bf57-3d6a59931322); in Scripture it appears as the chief city of [Aram](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000015), a trading city, a prophetic target, and the place where Saul of [Tarsus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000218) was converted and first preached Christ.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Damascus, capital of Syria

locationsMap.name: Daberath
locationsMap.title: Levitical town near [Mount Tabor](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000160) on the Issachar-Zebulun boundary
locationsMap.description: Daberath was a town on the boundary of Issachar and Zebulun and was assigned to the Gershonite Levites; it is commonly identified with Daburiyya on the western lower slopes of [Mount Tabor](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000160).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Daburiyya near Mount Tabor in northern Israel

locationsMap.name: Dalmanutha
locationsMap.title: uncertain Galilean destination named after the feeding of the four thousand
locationsMap.description: Dalmanutha is the destination named in [Mark 8:10](verse-key://MRK 8:10) after [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) fed the four thousand; it is probably somewhere on or near the western shore of the [Sea of Galilee](location-id://44329b87-3c5b-4d27-9fcf-e386f2aebc5b), often compared with Magdala or the Ginosar Plain, but the site remains disputed.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain; proposed near Magdala or the Ginosar Plain on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee

locationsMap.name: Dalmatia
locationsMap.title: Roman province and Adriatic region visited by [Titus](name-id://edebc9dd-3078-4022-b294-4ecd27682d47)
locationsMap.description: Dalmatia was a Roman imperial district on the eastern Adriatic coast, within the broader Illyrian world; [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) mentions that [Titus](name-id://edebc9dd-3078-4022-b294-4ecd27682d47) had gone there during the closing notices of [2 Timothy](book-key://2TI).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The eastern Adriatic coast, especially modern Croatia and neighboring coastal areas

locationsMap.name: Dan
locationsMap.title: northern Israelite city formerly called Laish and identified with Tel Dan
locationsMap.description: Dan was the northern city captured by Danites from Laish and renamed after their ancestor; it became a standard northern boundary marker in the phrase from Dan to [Beersheba](location-id://0643b4cb-a5f4-4af3-b469-ed061976d1f4) and was later associated with [Jeroboam](name-id://44442ff1-d137-4b0c-b117-4ccacc9df7f1)'s calf shrine.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Dan, also Tell el-Qadi, in northern Israel near the Lebanon border

locationsMap.name: Dannah
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) hill-country town probably represented by Idhna
locationsMap.description: Dannah is listed among towns in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) between Socoh and [Kiriath-sannah](location-id://68747049-f74c-420e-b466-6bdb5ab21514), which is [Debir](location-id://4fa90dfe-b09a-4872-8ba1-3cfadf500c44); older biblical geography identifies it probably with Idhna west of [Hebron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000103), though the identification remains probable rather than certain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Probably Idhna west of Hebron in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Debir
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) hill-country city also called Kirjathsepher and [Kirjathsannah](location-id://68747049-f74c-420e-b466-6bdb5ab21514)
locationsMap.description: This Debir was a royal Canaanite city in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119), also called Kirjathsepher and [Kirjathsannah](location-id://68747049-f74c-420e-b466-6bdb5ab21514); [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816) and later [Othniel](name-id://05427ab6-5c60-4277-bc79-556cb2bbbd31) are connected with its capture, and it was later assigned as a Levitical city.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Commonly associated with Khirbet Rabud southwest of Hebron, though older proposals include edh-Dhaheriyeh

locationsMap.name: Decapolis
locationsMap.title: Hellenistic league and district of cities east and south of [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080)
locationsMap.description: The Decapolis was a Greco-Roman group and district of cities in the southern Levant, chiefly east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987); the Gospels mention people from the Decapolis following [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) and Jesus' ministry passing through its region.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: A district of the southern Levant spanning parts of modern Jordan, Israel, and Syria

locationsMap.name: Dedan
locationsMap.title: north Arabian caravan oasis and kingdom associated with Dadan
locationsMap.description: Dedan in the prophetic books denotes the north Arabian caravan center and people of Dadan, later associated with Lihyan, whose trade and caravans are mentioned alongside [Arabia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000014), [Tyre](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000226), [Sheba](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000200), and related trading peoples.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Dadan at the al-Ula oasis in Medina Province, northwestern Saudi Arabia

locationsMap.name: Derbe
locationsMap.title: Lycaonian city visited by [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) and [Barnabas](name-id://ba3667d2-9c64-4e6e-8836-beb53828cb13)
locationsMap.description: Derbe was a city of [Lycaonia](location-id://5c29ab23-6d76-4fdf-be3b-4e2335bf187f) and later neighboring Anatolian regions; [Acts](book-key://ACT) names it in [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s missionary travel with [Barnabas](name-id://ba3667d2-9c64-4e6e-8836-beb53828cb13), and its most likely archaeological site is Kerti Huyuk northeast of Karaman, though that identification remains debated.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Most likely Kerti Huyuk near Ekinozu, northeast of Karaman in Turkey

locationsMap.name: Dibon
locationsMap.title: Moabite city also called Dibon-gad and identified with Dhiban
locationsMap.description: Dibon was a city north of the [Arnon](location-id://255578cb-f276-46f2-b857-683990b50518) that moved between Amorite, Israelite, and Moabite control; it is called Dibon-gad in the wilderness itinerary, appears in [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153) or Reuben-Gad contexts, and is identified with modern Dhiban where the Mesha Stele was found.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Dhiban in Madaba Governorate, Jordan

locationsMap.name: Dilean
locationsMap.title: unidentified Shephelah town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) near [Lachish](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000129) and [Eglon](location-id://42127334-9744-4a9d-8017-d33806005272)
locationsMap.description: Dilean was a town in the lowland or Shephelah of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) listed with Mizpeh and [Joktheel](location-id://78f0de4b-50f9-4194-88b4-e8ddf2e3e59a); older atlas sources place it probably north of [Lachish](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000129) and [Eglon](location-id://42127334-9744-4a9d-8017-d33806005272), but no secure modern identification is known.

locationsMap.name: Dimnah
locationsMap.title: Zebulun Levitical city probably preserving a Rimmon or Rimmono variant
locationsMap.description: Dimnah is listed in [Joshua 21:35](verse-key://JOS 21:35) as a city assigned to the Merarite Levites in Zebulun; many reference works treat the name as a textual variant or scribal error for Rimmon or Rimmono, commonly associated with modern Rummanah.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Probably Rummanah in northern Israel if Dimnah is the Rimmon/Rimmono variant

locationsMap.name: Dimonah
locationsMap.title: southern [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) town possibly connected with [Adadah](location-id://fb80498f-61e3-4bd9-b38a-de8ed5bfb015)
locationsMap.description: Dimonah is named among towns in the south of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) in [Joshua 15:22](verse-key://JOS 15:22); older atlas sources connect it with [Adadah](location-id://fb80498f-61e3-4bd9-b38a-de8ed5bfb015) and suggest locations southeast of [Beer-sheba](location-id://0643b4cb-a5f4-4af3-b469-ed061976d1f4) or [Arad](location-id://8ff2eef5-63cb-4e00-b463-fc226a98cfda), but the identification is not secure.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain; proposed near Ararah southeast of Beer-sheba or near Adadah southeast of Arad

locationsMap.name: Dinhabah
locationsMap.title: unidentified royal city of Bela king of [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064)
locationsMap.description: Dinhabah was the city of Bela son of Beor, the first king listed in [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064) before Israel had kings; no satisfactory modern identification has been proposed, and proposed resemblances such as Hodbat et-Teneib are geographically doubtful.

locationsMap.name: Dizahab
locationsMap.title: unidentified wilderness place in the opening setting of [Deuteronomy](book-key://DEU)
locationsMap.description: Dizahab appears in [Deuteronomy 1:1](verse-key://DEU 1:1) as part of the geographic description of [Moses](name-id://fff825ad-31e8-4843-a7dc-cd82e9878d73)' words beyond [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987); no place with a clearly matching name has been found, and suggestions such as Mina edh-Dhahab near the Gulf of Aqaba remain conjectural.

locationsMap.name: Dophkah
locationsMap.title: wilderness encampment between the wilderness of Sin and [Alush](location-id://f56d3c61-7c7b-43c0-b57e-e92514d4eb01)
locationsMap.description: Dophkah was one of Israel's wilderness stations, reached after the wilderness of Sin and before [Alush](location-id://f56d3c61-7c7b-43c0-b57e-e92514d4eb01) in the [Numbers 33](chapter-key://NUM 33) itinerary; no secure modern site has been identified.

locationsMap.name: Dor
locationsMap.title: Canaanite and coastal city south of [Mount Carmel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000154) identified with Tel Dor
locationsMap.description: Dor was a Canaanite royal city on the Mediterranean coast south of [Mount Carmel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000154), later associated with Manasseh's territory though not fully possessed by Israel; it is identified with Tel Dor near the former village of Tantura.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Dor on the Israeli coastal plain near Dor and Nahsholim

locationsMap.name: Dothan
locationsMap.title: northern Samarian site where [Joseph](name-id://207b40a3-2f5b-44bb-b90a-334cc21398b3) was sold and [Elisha](name-id://6e9af9e4-8635-4289-826f-bf6d37611683) was surrounded
locationsMap.description: Dothan is named in [Genesis](book-key://GEN) as the place where [Joseph](name-id://207b40a3-2f5b-44bb-b90a-334cc21398b3) found his brothers and was sold, and in Kings as the city where [Elisha](name-id://6e9af9e4-8635-4289-826f-bf6d37611683)'s servant saw the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire; modern consensus identifies it with Tel Dothan near Jenin.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Dothan, also Tell al-Hafireh, near Bir al-Basha southwest of Jenin in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Dragon Spring
locationsMap.title: lost spring or well in the Valley of Hinnom near [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: The Dragon Spring, rendered Dragon Well in the KJV, was a water source mentioned in Nehemiah's night inspection between the [Valley Gate](location-id://a1142449-1aa9-4dcd-ae43-388e5e0925d1) and the [Dung Gate](location-id://bcb91d43-fad0-45cf-8f9c-ccf48fb92d2c); it was probably in the Valley of Hinnom, but no extant source can be securely identified.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Unknown; probably somewhere in the Valley of Hinnom near Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Dumah
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) hill-country town identified with ed-Daume
locationsMap.description: This Dumah is the town listed in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) in [Joshua 15:52](verse-key://JOS 15:52); older biblical geography identifies it with ed-Daume in the southern hill country between [Hebron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000103) and [Beer-sheba](location-id://0643b4cb-a5f4-4af3-b469-ed061976d1f4).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: ed-Daume in the southern hill country of Judah

locationsMap.name: Dung Gate
locationsMap.title: [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) gate near the refuse route toward the Valley of Hinnom
locationsMap.description: The Dung Gate in [Nehemiah](book-key://NEH) was a gate of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) near the route toward the Valley of Hinnom, probably named for refuse taken from the temple area and burned outside the city; the modern Old City Dung Gate preserves the name but is a later Ottoman gate and not necessarily the exact ancient opening.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ancient location near Jerusalem's southern wall and the Valley of Hinnom; the modern Dung Gate is in the Old City wall

locationsMap.name: Dura
locationsMap.title: Babylonian plain where [Nebuchadnezzar](name-id://4f085903-eda2-4736-9163-a6136ad71000) set up the golden image
locationsMap.description: Dura was the plain in the province of [Babylon](location-id://8939f721-e16f-4837-84f0-ec3dcc65ea70) where [Nebuchadnezzar](name-id://4f085903-eda2-4736-9163-a6136ad71000) set up the golden image in [Daniel 3](chapter-key://DAN 3); its exact location is disputed, with suggestions ranging from a site near Babylon to a broader reference to a rampart or plain within the Babylonian district.

locationsMap.name: Edom
locationsMap.title: kingdom and region south of the Dead Sea associated with [Esau](name-id://c4d0e1b7-7cba-49cb-80b6-e5068cfb4e2f)
locationsMap.description: Edom was the territory and kingdom east and south of the [Arabah](location-id://bfd23a68-b7bd-4bd0-99fe-d1d16a0b2a71), associated in the Bible with [Esau](name-id://c4d0e1b7-7cba-49cb-80b6-e5068cfb4e2f) and the Edomites; its biblical landscape includes [Seir](location-id://3fc9393f-3978-40df-9a42-b7bc33401f98), [Bozrah](location-id://5269e4ff-e6d7-4775-a881-29415029f4e9), [Elath](location-id://127d2c12-56b6-426a-abef-d7036d3f4ab5), and [Eziongeber](location-id://8780e2a1-8c59-4de3-9fa1-aaa3b332ecb4).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Southern Jordan and the Arabah region south and southeast of the Dead Sea

locationsMap.name: Egypt
locationsMap.title: Nile land and kingdom central to the patriarchal and Exodus narratives
locationsMap.description: Egypt is the Nile land repeatedly named in Scripture as a refuge, empire, trading partner, place of Israelite bondage, and prophetic subject; the biblical name covers ancient Egypt rather than only the modern state.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Egypt, especially the Nile Valley and Nile Delta

locationsMap.name: Ekron
locationsMap.title: Philistine city identified with Tel Miqne
locationsMap.description: Ekron was one of the five Philistine cities, assigned on Israelite boundary lists but known especially as a Philistine center, the place associated with Baalzebub, and a major Iron Age olive-oil production site.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Miqne/Khirbet el-Muqanna in Israel

locationsMap.name: Elam
locationsMap.title: ancient region and kingdom in southwestern Iran
locationsMap.description: Elam was an ancient region and kingdom east of [Babylonia](location-id://a4fdc004-f375-4bf2-a0ad-8d77ec7fce98), often centered in Susiana and the Iranian highlands; in Scripture it appears in [Genesis](book-key://GEN), prophetic oracles, and Daniel.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Khuzestan and adjacent highland areas of southwestern Iran

locationsMap.name: Elim
locationsMap.title: Exodus oasis with twelve wells and seventy palm trees
locationsMap.description: Elim was an Israelite encampment after [Marah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000144) and before the wilderness of Sin, described in [Exodus](book-key://EXO) and [Numbers](book-key://NUM) as having twelve wells of water and seventy palm trees; proposed sites include Wadi Gharandel and Uyun Musa.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Often proposed as Wadi Gharandel or Uyun Musa in the Sinai, but the identification is disputed

locationsMap.name: Emmaus
locationsMap.title: village near [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) on the road where the risen [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) appeared
locationsMap.description: Emmaus is the village named in [Luke 24](chapter-key://LUK 24) where two disciples recognized the risen [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab); its exact site is disputed, with proposed identifications including Emmaus Nicopolis, al-Qubeiba, Abu Ghosh, and Motza.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Disputed; often proposed as Imwas/Emmaus Nicopolis or al-Qubeiba in the Jerusalem region

locationsMap.name: Engedi
locationsMap.title: Dead Sea oasis and wilderness stronghold of [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)
locationsMap.description: Engedi, KJV Engedi, was an oasis and settlement on the western shore of the Dead Sea, identified with [Hazazon-tamar](location-id://01cbbee4-41b6-442f-a7c1-a64c15f9542f) and associated with [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) hiding from [Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb), [Jehoshaphat](name-id://3a573bf3-3bda-458d-b7ac-5b2e4f3205f6), and the imagery of [Song of Solomon](book-key://SNG) and [Ezekiel](book-key://EZK).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ein Gedi oasis and archaeological site on the western shore of the Dead Sea in Israel

locationsMap.name: Eshcol
locationsMap.title: valley near [Hebron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000103) where Israelite spies cut a grape cluster
locationsMap.description: Eshcol is the valley or brook where the spies sent from [Kadesh](location-id://501d3b61-a4e6-4e1e-82b1-f8799fb77131) cut down a cluster of grapes as evidence of [Canaan](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000045)'s fruitfulness; it is generally placed in the [Hebron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000103) region, but the exact valley is uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Probably a valley in the Hebron area of the southern hill country

locationsMap.name: Ethiopia
locationsMap.title: biblical [Cush](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000059) or Ethiopia south of [Egypt](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000065)
locationsMap.description: KJV Ethiopia usually represents [Cush](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000059), the Nile region south of [Egypt](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000065) known to the biblical writers through Nubia and related lands; it should not be treated as identical with only the modern state of Ethiopia.
