locationsMap.modernIdentification: Nubia and the Upper Nile region of Sudan and southern Egypt, with broader ancient associations to Cush

locationsMap.name: East Gate
locationsMap.title: eastern gate associated with [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) temple access
locationsMap.description: The East Gate in [Nehemiah](book-key://NEH) is the gate watched by Shemaiah during the rebuilding of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117); related east-facing temple gates also appear in [Ezekiel](book-key://EZK) and later temple tradition.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Approximate eastern side of the Jerusalem temple area

locationsMap.name: Ebenezer
locationsMap.title: unidentified Israelite battle site and [Samuel](name-id://1f1722fd-38b9-474c-9c94-fcbeb1d47812) memorial stone
locationsMap.description: Ebenezer names both the site near Aphek where Israel fought the Philistines and the memorial stone [Samuel](name-id://1f1722fd-38b9-474c-9c94-fcbeb1d47812) later set between Mizpeh and [Shen](location-id://8444f423-821d-43c0-b789-8bbf11e48e42); neither exact location is securely identified.

locationsMap.name: Eder of Judah
locationsMap.title: southern town in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) distinct from the Tower of Eder
locationsMap.description: Eder of Judah is listed among the far southern towns of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) near [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064) in [Joshua 15:21](verse-key://JOS 15:21); it is distinct from the Tower of Eder in [Genesis](book-key://GEN), and its site is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Edrei
locationsMap.title: [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d) city of King [Og](name-id://4c740990-dad3-4d94-b039-f55ed02efa7b) identified with Daraa
locationsMap.description: Edrei of [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d) was one of the cities of [Og](name-id://4c740990-dad3-4d94-b039-f55ed02efa7b) and the place associated with his defeat by Israel; it is normally identified with Daraa in southern [Syria](location-id://f4fe75e3-4f92-4642-bf57-3d6a59931322).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Daraa, Syria

locationsMap.name: Eglaim
locationsMap.title: Moabite site also associated with En-eglaim
locationsMap.description: Eglaim is named in Isaiah's oracle against [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153) and is commonly associated in atlas tradition with En-eglaim of [Ezekiel 47:10](verse-key://EZK 47:10); the exact site in Moab or near the Dead Sea is not identified.

locationsMap.name: Eglon
locationsMap.title: Canaanite royal city in the Shephelah of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Eglon was a Canaanite royal city whose king joined the southern coalition against [Gibeon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000088) and was later conquered by [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816); suggested sites include Khirbet Ajlan and Tell Nejileh, so the exact identification remains uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Usually sought in the Shephelah near Lachish, but the site is disputed

locationsMap.name: Elbethel
locationsMap.title: altar-site at [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032) named by [Jacob](name-id://23ed64d8-8458-49af-9b51-f578ab3262d9)
locationsMap.description: Elbethel is the name [Jacob](name-id://23ed64d8-8458-49af-9b51-f578ab3262d9) gave to the altar he built at [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032) after God appeared to him there; it is a sacred place-name within the Bethel site rather than a separate city.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Bethel, commonly identified with Beitin in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Elparan
locationsMap.title: place by the wilderness of [Paran](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000177) reached by [Chedorlaomer](name-id://ed428395-dc41-4ed2-9229-bd7abfaa930f)
locationsMap.description: Elparan is named in [Genesis 14:6](verse-key://GEN 14:6) as a place by the wilderness after the invaders smote the Horites in [Seir](location-id://3fc9393f-3978-40df-9a42-b7bc33401f98); older atlas tradition connects it with the [Elath](location-id://127d2c12-56b6-426a-abef-d7036d3f4ab5) region, but the identification is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Elath
locationsMap.title: Edomite and Judahite [Red Sea](location-id://26deae24-2471-47c1-8280-28e380224f20) port near [Eziongeber](location-id://8780e2a1-8c59-4de3-9fa1-aaa3b332ecb4)
locationsMap.description: Elath, also spelled Eloth, was a Red Sea port associated with [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064), [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119), [Solomon](name-id://509b7c2f-b8bf-4a4d-a393-550a7a4b259f)'s fleets, and the Gulf of Aqaba; it lay near [Eziongeber](location-id://8780e2a1-8c59-4de3-9fa1-aaa3b332ecb4) and is commonly connected with the Aqaba/Eilat area.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Aqaba/Eilat at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba

locationsMap.name: Elealeh
locationsMap.title: Reubenite and Moabite town north of [Heshbon](location-id://fcdae541-01d2-47f8-a663-45a2f056a250)
locationsMap.description: Elealeh was rebuilt by Reuben and later appears in prophetic oracles over [Moab](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000153) together with [Heshbon](location-id://fcdae541-01d2-47f8-a663-45a2f056a250); it is represented by el-Al, about a mile north of Heshbon.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: el-Al near Hisban in Jordan

locationsMap.name: Elishah
locationsMap.title: islands or maritime region supplying dyed cloth to [Tyre](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000226)
locationsMap.description: Elishah is named among the descendants of [Javan](name-id://7065e0a8-dc87-453c-acb8-bccc4d2ebab7) and in [Ezekiel](book-key://EZK) as the source of blue and purple goods for [Tyre](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000226); proposed identifications include [Cyprus](location-id://cddb5c4a-d659-447d-b7bd-cd2aee99dde2), [Greece](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000094), Italy, and other Aegean or Mediterranean regions, but no certainty is possible.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Often associated with Cyprus or the Aegean, but uncertain

locationsMap.name: Ellasar
locationsMap.title: kingdom of [Arioch](name-id://76a5f4c8-73ac-4b79-b2de-49e78a23c82f), often identified with Larsa
locationsMap.description: Ellasar was the kingdom of [Arioch](name-id://76a5f4c8-73ac-4b79-b2de-49e78a23c82f) in [Genesis 14](chapter-key://GEN 14); many older lexicons and atlases identify it with Larsa in southern [Babylonia](location-id://a4fdc004-f375-4bf2-a0ad-8d77ec7fce98), though the biblical equation remains debated.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Probably Larsa/Tell as-Senkereh in southern Iraq

locationsMap.name: Elon
locationsMap.title: Danite town possibly related to [Elon-beth-hanan](location-id://68a1f304-f4e7-4bcf-9d0e-fe4e0c13265d)
locationsMap.description: Elon is listed among towns in the territory of Dan between Ithlah and [Timnah](location-id://023d7831-a16e-417f-b7b2-ddaa748aa2b9); it may be related to [Elon-beth-hanan](location-id://68a1f304-f4e7-4bcf-9d0e-fe4e0c13265d), but its location is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Elonbethhanan
locationsMap.title: Solomonic district town possibly identical with [Elon](location-id://788b7879-57b1-474e-a254-5b8457791861)
locationsMap.description: Elonbethhanan, KJV Elon-beth-hanan, appears in [Solomon](name-id://509b7c2f-b8bf-4a4d-a393-550a7a4b259f)'s administrative districts together with [Shaalbim](location-id://4413d56c-bdd0-455a-8cbc-9f64e00baae6) and [Beth-shemesh](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000037); it may be identical with [Elon](location-id://788b7879-57b1-474e-a254-5b8457791861), but the identification is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Eltekeh
locationsMap.title: Danite and Levitical town probably near [Beth-horon](location-id://1724eb98-7344-46c9-b069-6d0db1d09f5c)
locationsMap.description: Eltekeh, also spelled Elteke, was a town of Dan given to the Kohathite Levites; it may be the Assyrian Altaqu and is usually sought east of [Ekron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000066), but the site is not certain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Possibly Beit Liqya or another site east of Ekron

locationsMap.name: Eltekon
locationsMap.title: unidentified hill-country town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Eltekon is named in [Joshua 15:59](verse-key://JOS 15:59) among towns in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) near [Beth-anoth](location-id://3ff1c8e1-8f0f-47d7-acd2-e5c1bf7ec27e); no secure modern site is known.

locationsMap.name: Eltolad
locationsMap.title: southern [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) town later assigned to Simeon
locationsMap.description: Eltolad was a Negeb town listed for [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and then within the Simeonite inheritance; it is probably the [Tolad](location-id://51818329-468d-4463-a10d-58358fb143f5) of [1 Chronicles 4:29](verse-key://1CH 4:29), but the site is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Endor
locationsMap.title: Manasseh town near [Mount Tabor](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000160) associated with [Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb)
locationsMap.description: Endor was a town in the allotment of Manasseh, remembered for [Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb) consulting the woman with a familiar spirit there and for [Psalm 83](chapter-key://PSA 83); it is commonly identified with Indur near [Mount Tabor](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000160).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Indur in northern Israel

locationsMap.name: En Gannim of Issachar
locationsMap.title: Issachar and Levitical town commonly identified with Jenin
locationsMap.description: En Gannim of Issachar was assigned to Issachar and later to the Gershonite Levites; it is commonly identified with Jenin, whose name preserves the idea of gardens or springs.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Jenin in the northern West Bank

locationsMap.name: Enhaddah
locationsMap.title: Issachar town of uncertain site
locationsMap.description: Enhaddah is listed among the towns of Issachar in [Joshua 19:21](verse-key://JOS 19:21); the place is not otherwise described and its modern identification is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Enhakkore
locationsMap.title: spring at Lehi named after [Samson](name-id://cc81f251-0c5e-452d-9ae8-5b96db780648) called to God
locationsMap.description: Enhakkore is the spring God opened for [Samson](name-id://cc81f251-0c5e-452d-9ae8-5b96db780648) after the battle at Lehi; the narrative names it at Lehi, but no independent modern site is secure.

locationsMap.name: Enhazor
locationsMap.title: Naphtali town listed near [Kedesh](location-id://1f447b5c-761c-4a77-bd5c-309916278396) and [Edrei](location-id://51baf351-58c2-46bd-b073-98b785cb48fc)
locationsMap.description: Enhazor is named in the allotment of Naphtali near [Kedesh](location-id://1f447b5c-761c-4a77-bd5c-309916278396) and [Edrei](location-id://51baf351-58c2-46bd-b073-98b785cb48fc); suggested identifications exist in upper [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080), but the exact site remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Enmishpat
locationsMap.title: older name for [Kadesh](location-id://501d3b61-a4e6-4e1e-82b1-f8799fb77131) in the wilderness south of [Canaan](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000045)
locationsMap.description: Enmishpat is identified in [Genesis 14:7](verse-key://GEN 14:7) as [Kadesh](location-id://501d3b61-a4e6-4e1e-82b1-f8799fb77131), the place reached by [Chedorlaomer](name-id://ed428395-dc41-4ed2-9229-bd7abfaa930f) before striking the Amalekites and Amorites; the broader Kadeshbarnea location is debated.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Kadesh-Barnea region, often associated with Ain el-Qudeirat or nearby springs

locationsMap.name: Enrimmon
locationsMap.title: postexilic [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) settlement combining Ain and Rimmon
locationsMap.description: Enrimmon appears in [Nehemiah 11:29](verse-key://NEH 11:29) among towns resettled by [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119); it is usually understood as the combined Ain-Rimmon of the southern Judah/Simeon lists, but the exact site is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Enrogel
locationsMap.title: spring on the [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) boundary near the [Kidron](location-id://1b95372c-c14a-4b30-a247-cad60acefe7c) and Hinnom valleys
locationsMap.description: Enrogel was a boundary spring between [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) and later a place connected with [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)'s messengers and [Adonijah](name-id://a56a9032-8c0f-4140-b3b1-50905b9933ba)'s feast; it is commonly identified with Bir Ayyub, Job's Well, south of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Bir Ayyub, Job's Well, near the junction of the Kidron and Hinnom valleys

locationsMap.name: Enshemesh
locationsMap.title: spring on the [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)-[Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) border east of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: Enshemesh was a spring on the boundary between [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef), named between [Enrogel](location-id://da88cd17-047b-4fcc-bcfc-d1a01b0abbd8) and [Adummim](location-id://147db671-a765-4d7f-b250-b6614116bef2); it is usually sought east of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117), but the exact spring is debated.

locationsMap.name: Entappuah
locationsMap.title: spring of [Tappuah](location-id://e753363e-0928-4ea3-b304-cf335a24ab2a) on the Manasseh-Ephraim border
locationsMap.description: Entappuah is named in [Joshua 17:7](verse-key://JOS 17:7) on the border of Manasseh near [Tappuah](location-id://e753363e-0928-4ea3-b304-cf335a24ab2a); the site belongs to the central hill-country border geography, but its exact spring is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Enam
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) town in the Shephelah possibly related to Enaim
locationsMap.description: Enam is listed among towns in the Shephelah of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119); some connect it with Enaim in [Genesis](book-key://GEN), but the site is not securely identified.

locationsMap.name: Ephah
locationsMap.title: Midianite tribal region named with [Midian](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000152) in [Isaiah](book-key://ISA)
locationsMap.description: Ephah is primarily a Midianite clan name, but [Isaiah 60:6](verse-key://ISA 60:6) uses it alongside [Midian](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000152) in a geographic-ethnic setting; the corresponding territory is not securely located.

locationsMap.name: Ephesdammim
locationsMap.title: Philistine camp between Socoh and [Azekah](location-id://f345fc22-3282-4ad7-9817-3e2b38026e41)
locationsMap.description: Ephesdammim, KJV Ephesdammim, was the Philistine encampment between Socoh and [Azekah](location-id://f345fc22-3282-4ad7-9817-3e2b38026e41) before [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) fought [Goliath](name-id://69bffebc-acde-4cc2-83a4-cc0533c60424); no exact modern locality is secure.

locationsMap.name: Ephesus
locationsMap.title: Roman Asian city central to [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) and [Revelation](book-key://REV)
locationsMap.description: Ephesus was an ancient city on the coast of Ionia in western Asia Minor, later inland from the coast; in the New Testament it was a major center of [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s ministry and one of the seven churches of [Revelation](book-key://REV).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ephesus archaeological site near Selcuk, Izmir Province, Turkey

locationsMap.name: Ephraim
locationsMap.title: city near the wilderness where [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) withdrew
locationsMap.description: The city called Ephraim in [John 11:54](verse-key://JHN 11:54) lay near the wilderness north of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117); it is usually identified with et-Taiyibeh, though the identification is not absolutely certain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Usually et-Taiyibeh northeast of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Ephrath
locationsMap.title: ancient name associated with [Bethlehem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000034) and [Rachel](name-id://84d78b89-880b-4333-a822-9c8449f77fd0)'s burial
locationsMap.description: Ephrath, also Ephrathah or KJV Ephratah, is associated with [Bethlehem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000034) and the road where [Rachel](name-id://84d78b89-880b-4333-a822-9c8449f77fd0) was buried; some sources regard the Rachel-burial references as a distinct place, so the identification remains partly uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Bethlehem area in the West Bank, with some uncertainty for the Rachel-burial references

locationsMap.name: Erech
locationsMap.title: ancient city of [Shinar](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000204) identified with Uruk
locationsMap.description: Erech was one of [Nimrod](name-id://80b191de-d8ed-486d-bbb5-bd36756496ac)'s cities in [Shinar](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000204) and is identified with Uruk, the major ancient city represented by Warka in southern Iraq.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uruk/Warka in Muthanna Governorate, Iraq

locationsMap.name: Esek
locationsMap.title: well near [Gerar](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000086) named for contention
locationsMap.description: Esek was the well dug by [Isaac](name-id://a5b2f874-2008-4b28-9698-6357fe71c3bf)'s servants and disputed by the herdsmen of [Gerar](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000086); the well lay in the Gerar region, but the exact site is not identified.

locationsMap.name: Eshtaol
locationsMap.title: Danite border town associated with [Samson](name-id://cc81f251-0c5e-452d-9ae8-5b96db780648)
locationsMap.description: Eshtaol was a town on the Dan-Judah border, associated with the camp of Dan, [Samson](name-id://cc81f251-0c5e-452d-9ae8-5b96db780648)'s early stirrings, his burial between [Zorah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000244) and Eshtaol, and the Danite migration narrative.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Eshtaol in the Jerusalem District of Israel

locationsMap.name: Eshtemoa
locationsMap.title: Levitical town in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Eshtemoa, also spelled Eshtemoh in [Joshua 15:50](verse-key://JOS 15:50), was a town in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) assigned to the Levites and later among the places to which [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) sent spoil; it is identified with es-Samu south of [Hebron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000103).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: as-Samu south of Hebron in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Etam of Judah
locationsMap.title: fortified [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) town near [Bethlehem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000034) and [Tekoa](location-id://4a075a4d-bb20-4a0e-a4e4-bbe3c9acdb97)
locationsMap.description: Etam of Judah is named among the cities fortified by [Rehoboam](name-id://68d5eac0-52b9-4b0b-b484-8c7b5c3b8971) between [Bethlehem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000034) and [Tekoa](location-id://4a075a4d-bb20-4a0e-a4e4-bbe3c9acdb97) and is often connected with the spring area near Artas, though the exact ancient town site is not certain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Probably near Artas and Ain Atan south of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Etham
locationsMap.title: Exodus encampment at the edge of the wilderness
locationsMap.description: Etham was an Israelite encampment after [Succoth](location-id://f577cd82-77ac-4216-8c7d-86b5dd1bb0b3) and before the turn toward [Pihahiroth](location-id://179225ab-e39e-4379-88aa-105442a791e3); [Numbers](book-key://NUM) also names the wilderness of Etham after the sea crossing, but the precise route location is disputed.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Often placed near the north end of the Bitter Lakes or eastern Nile Delta route, but uncertain

locationsMap.name: Ether
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) town later assigned to Simeon near [Libnah](location-id://70d91d4d-8075-4ffe-9d3b-0571ec07539c) and [Ashan](location-id://a996092a-1f04-4e3f-a1e4-a867de330047)
locationsMap.description: Ether was a town in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) near [Libnah](location-id://70d91d4d-8075-4ffe-9d3b-0571ec07539c) and [Ashan](location-id://a996092a-1f04-4e3f-a1e4-a867de330047) and later appears in the Simeonite allotment; Khirbet el-Atr has been suggested, but the identification is not certain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Possibly Khirbet el-Atr near Beit Jibrin

locationsMap.name: Euphrates
locationsMap.title: great river of [Mesopotamia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000151) marking biblical boundaries and routes
locationsMap.description: The Euphrates is the great river of [Mesopotamia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000151), named from Eden and the patriarchal promises through Israelite royal history, prophetic symbolism, and [Revelation](book-key://REV).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Euphrates River flowing through Turkey, Syria, and Iraq

locationsMap.name: Ezem
locationsMap.title: southern [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and Simeon town of uncertain site
locationsMap.description: Ezem, also rendered Azem in some traditions, was a southern [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) town later included in Simeon; its exact site is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Eziongeber
locationsMap.title: [Red Sea](location-id://26deae24-2471-47c1-8280-28e380224f20) port near [Elath](location-id://127d2c12-56b6-426a-abef-d7036d3f4ab5) used by [Solomon](name-id://509b7c2f-b8bf-4a4d-a393-550a7a4b259f) and [Jehoshaphat](name-id://3a573bf3-3bda-458d-b7ac-5b2e4f3205f6)
locationsMap.description: Eziongeber was an encampment and later a Red Sea port beside [Eloth](location-id://127d2c12-56b6-426a-abef-d7036d3f4ab5) in the land of [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064), associated with [Solomon](name-id://509b7c2f-b8bf-4a4d-a393-550a7a4b259f)'s and [Jehoshaphat](name-id://3a573bf3-3bda-458d-b7ac-5b2e4f3205f6)'s maritime ventures; its precise site near the head of the Gulf of Aqaba is debated.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Near the head of the Gulf of Aqaba, possibly north of modern Aqaba/Eilat

locationsMap.name: Fair Havens
locationsMap.title: Cretan roadstead where [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s ship paused on the voyage to [Rome](location-id://ff427d76-a9e7-4a50-bc2d-61b6b459e87b)
locationsMap.description: Fair Havens was a roadstead on the south coast of [Crete](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000055), near the city of [Lasea](location-id://7d4efebb-91ba-4bf8-9b5a-509080945c86), where [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s Alexandrian ship arrived with difficulty before the crew debated whether to winter there or sail on toward Phenice.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Kaloi Limenes or Kali Limenes on the south coast of Crete, Greece

locationsMap.name: Field of Blood
locationsMap.title: [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) field associated with [Judas](name-id://04da74b8-9c6e-4d10-b3a0-e98df6bd6b97) and the potter's field
locationsMap.description: The Field of Blood, called Aceldama in the KJV of [Acts](book-key://ACT), was the field associated with [Judas](name-id://04da74b8-9c6e-4d10-b3a0-e98df6bd6b97)'s betrayal money and the potter's field bought for burying strangers; Christian tradition locates it on the south side of the [Valley of Hinnom](location-id://a1d1ba7a-4860-43ea-8b07-7ed384708492) near its junction with the Kidron Valley.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Akeldama near St. Onuphrius Monastery south of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Fish Gate
locationsMap.title: [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) gate named in [Manasseh](name-id://cb3e0962-0140-4360-8730-0cc3c09a21da)'s wall and [Nehemiah](name-id://46c4c07f-dde8-4466-a278-6e40a8d3e7f1)'s repairs
locationsMap.description: The Fish Gate was a gate of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) named in [Manasseh](name-id://cb3e0962-0140-4360-8730-0cc3c09a21da)'s outer wall, rebuilt in [Nehemiah](name-id://46c4c07f-dde8-4466-a278-6e40a8d3e7f1)'s wall repairs, passed in the dedication procession, and mentioned in [Zephaniah](name-id://f4faf4ff-7333-4763-8cf8-7954f40f88eb)'s oracle; its exact position is usually placed on the northern or northwestern side of ancient Jerusalem but remains uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Approximate northern or northwestern sector of ancient Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Forum of Appius
locationsMap.title: Appian Way market town where Roman believers met [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)
locationsMap.description: The Forum of Appius, KJV Appii forum, was a town and road station on the Appian Way about forty-three Roman miles southeast of [Rome](location-id://ff427d76-a9e7-4a50-bc2d-61b6b459e87b); Roman believers came there and to the [Three Taverns](location-id://0873a885-e83e-4438-a9c7-20bd5515118c) to meet [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) on his journey to Rome.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ruins near Treponti in Lazio, Italy

locationsMap.name: Fountain Gate
locationsMap.title: [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) gate near the king's pool and City of David stairs
locationsMap.description: The Fountain Gate, called the spring gate in some English renderings, was a [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) gate visited by [Nehemiah](name-id://46c4c07f-dde8-4466-a278-6e40a8d3e7f1), repaired by Shallun, and passed in the dedication procession; Nehemiah places it near the king's pool, the pool of Shelah, the king's garden, and the stairs descending from the City of David.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Approximate southeastern sector of ancient Jerusalem near the City of David and Siloam area

locationsMap.name: Galilee
locationsMap.title: northern region of Palestine central to [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab)' ministry
locationsMap.description: Galilee was the northern region of Palestine west of the [Sea of Galilee](location-id://44329b87-3c5b-4d27-9fcf-e386f2aebc5b), including towns such as [Nazareth](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000167), [Cana](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000044), and [Capernaum](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000046); in the New Testament it is the main setting of [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab)' early ministry and many post-resurrection references.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Galilee region of northern Israel

locationsMap.name: Garden of Eden
locationsMap.title: primordial garden planted eastward in Eden
locationsMap.description: The Garden of Eden is the garden of [Genesis](book-key://GEN) where God placed the first humans and from which a river is said to divide into four heads; its geographical location has been debated since antiquity and cannot be fixed securely from the biblical data.

locationsMap.name: Gath
locationsMap.title: Philistine city associated with [Goliath](name-id://69bffebc-acde-4cc2-83a4-cc0533c60424) and [Achish](name-id://cdba8edc-48d4-4a2c-af2a-138d3a881b0a)
locationsMap.description: Gath was one of the five chief Philistine cities, the home of [Goliath](name-id://69bffebc-acde-4cc2-83a4-cc0533c60424) and the city ruled by [Achish](name-id://cdba8edc-48d4-4a2c-af2a-138d3a881b0a) where [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) took refuge; it is commonly identified with Tell es-Safi in the Shephelah.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell es-Safi in central Israel

locationsMap.name: Gaza
locationsMap.title: Philistine city on the southern coastal plain
locationsMap.description: Gaza was a major city of the Philistines near the southern coast, named in boundary lists, [Samson](name-id://cc81f251-0c5e-452d-9ae8-5b96db780648) narratives, prophetic oracles, and the road direction in [Acts 8](chapter-key://ACT 8).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Gaza City in the Gaza Strip

locationsMap.name: Gerar
locationsMap.title: Philistine-region city associated with [Abraham](name-id://4ce14dfc-b652-45d9-ac05-5f0cf716c412) and [Isaac](name-id://a5b2f874-2008-4b28-9698-6357fe71c3bf)
locationsMap.description: Gerar was the city or district ruled by [Abimelech](name-id://eba375fa-1ab3-473b-85e6-f85f0771669c) where [Abraham](name-id://4ce14dfc-b652-45d9-ac05-5f0cf716c412) and later [Isaac](name-id://a5b2f874-2008-4b28-9698-6357fe71c3bf) sojourned; its precise site is disputed, though it is usually sought in the northwestern Negev or southern coastal plain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Often associated with the Tell Abu Hureirah or Umm Jerrar area in the northwestern Negev, but not securely fixed

locationsMap.name: Gethsemane
locationsMap.title: garden place across [Kidron](location-id://1b95372c-c14a-4b30-a247-cad60acefe7c) on the [Mount of Olives](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000158)
locationsMap.description: Gethsemane was the place where [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) prayed before his arrest, located across the [Kidron](location-id://1b95372c-c14a-4b30-a247-cad60acefe7c) in the [Mount of Olives](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000158) area; the traditional garden preserves the general setting, while the exact ancient spot is uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Traditional Garden of Gethsemane on the western slope of the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Gibeon
locationsMap.title: Hivite city northwest of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) identified with el-Jib
locationsMap.description: Gibeon was the chief city of the Gibeonites who made covenant with Israel, later a Levitical city and the site of major conflicts and worship; it is securely associated with el-Jib northwest of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: el-Jib in the West Bank, northwest of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Gilead
locationsMap.title: east-Jordan highland region known for balm and pastoral land
locationsMap.description: Gilead was the mountainous east-Jordan region associated with the tribes of [Reuben](name-id://93b5d553-bee9-4897-a61d-2a5878e1c10b), [Gad](name-id://b68edd6a-6aea-4f9f-8c99-684d9a6f7a8b), and [Manasseh](name-id://6d826bc2-ac80-4c27-af89-258a50f37dfe), with pastoral wealth, balm, and repeated military and prophetic references.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The highlands east of the Jordan River, chiefly in northwestern Jordan

locationsMap.name: Golgotha
locationsMap.title: place of [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab)' crucifixion outside [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)
locationsMap.description: Golgotha, interpreted as the place of a skull, was the site outside [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) where [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) was crucified; the broad Jerusalem setting is clear, but the exact site is disputed between traditional and alternative identifications.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Jerusalem, with the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and Garden Tomb among proposed identifications

locationsMap.name: Gomorrah
locationsMap.title: city of the plain destroyed with [Sodom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000212)
locationsMap.description: Gomorrah was one of the cities of the plain destroyed in the [Genesis](book-key://GEN) judgment narrative and later used as a byword for devastation; its exact site is unknown, often sought near the Dead Sea.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain site in the Dead Sea region

locationsMap.name: Goshen
locationsMap.title: Egyptian district where [Jacob](name-id://23ed64d8-8458-49af-9b51-f578ab3262d9)'s family settled
locationsMap.description: Goshen was the fertile district of [Egypt](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000065) where [Joseph](name-id://207b40a3-2f5b-44bb-b90a-334cc21398b3) settled [Jacob](name-id://23ed64d8-8458-49af-9b51-f578ab3262d9)'s family and where Israel dwelt before the Exodus; it is usually associated with the eastern Nile Delta, though its exact boundaries are debated.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Eastern Nile Delta of Egypt, often connected with Wadi Tumilat and the area around ancient Avaris and Pi-Ramesses

locationsMap.name: Goshen (city in Judah)
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) hill-country town named with [Giloh](location-id://cfac9a67-5a8a-42bf-be72-93c82d77bbe6) and [Arab](location-id://b5e2c349-1cd7-4bc8-8ba9-9b6ace77feda)
locationsMap.description: The city of Goshen in [Joshua 15:51](verse-key://JOS 15:51) was a town in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)'s hill-country list, distinct from the Egyptian region and the broader Goshen country in southern Judah; its site is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Great Sea
locationsMap.title: KJV name for the Mediterranean Sea west of [Canaan](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000045)
locationsMap.description: The Great Sea is the Mediterranean Sea, repeatedly used as the western boundary marker for Israel's land in the wilderness, conquest, and prophetic boundary texts.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Mediterranean Sea

locationsMap.name: Greece
locationsMap.title: Hellenic region called Grecia in [Daniel](book-key://DAN) and [Zechariah](book-key://ZEC)
locationsMap.description: Greece, called Grecia in several KJV prophetic passages, is the Hellenic world opposed to [Persia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000181) in [Daniel](book-key://DAN) and later visited by [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) in [Acts](book-key://ACT).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Greece and the wider ancient Hellenic world

locationsMap.name: Gaash
locationsMap.title: mountain or hill country near [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816)'s burial place
locationsMap.description: Gaash was the mountain or hill country on the north side of [Timnathserah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000222) where [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816) was buried; the name also appears in warrior lists, but the exact site is not securely identified.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain hill country near Timnath-serah in Ephraim

locationsMap.name: Gabbatha
locationsMap.title: pavement in [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) where [Pilate](name-id://753d1b13-3496-4ef1-b788-7825a59b5b36) judged [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab)
locationsMap.description: Gabbatha, also called the Pavement or Lithostrotos, was the judgment place where [Pilate](name-id://753d1b13-3496-4ef1-b788-7825a59b5b36) sat when [Jesus](name-id://354b61f9-94df-4810-9b87-065b029810ab) was presented before crucifixion; the exact location within Roman [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) is disputed.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain pavement or tribunal area in Roman Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Galatia
locationsMap.title: central Anatolian region addressed in [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223)'s ministry and letter
locationsMap.description: Galatia was the Anatolian region and Roman provincial sphere visited by [Paul](name-id://f5a4422f-ceeb-4400-a563-ea126def1223) and addressed in the Epistle to the Galatians; the exact scope intended in the letter is debated, but the biblical region is in Asia Minor.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Central Anatolia in modern Turkey

locationsMap.name: Galeed
locationsMap.title: [Jacob](name-id://23ed64d8-8458-49af-9b51-f578ab3262d9) and [Laban](name-id://02b09a01-9819-4182-895a-b0dda2395250)'s witness heap in [Gilead](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000089)
locationsMap.description: Galeed was the name [Jacob](name-id://23ed64d8-8458-49af-9b51-f578ab3262d9) gave to the heap of witness raised with [Laban](name-id://02b09a01-9819-4182-895a-b0dda2395250) in the hill country of [Gilead](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000089); the narrative fixes the general Gilead setting but not a recoverable archaeological site.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain place in the Gilead region east of the Jordan

locationsMap.name: Gallim
locationsMap.title: [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef)-area village named in [Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb) and Isaiah traditions
locationsMap.description: Gallim was the home associated with [Phalti](name-id://04b4f116-90d5-4c60-8375-9f5f7ed4d456) after [Michal](name-id://37d5ac9f-b6fc-47ed-8983-4c21dbf04085) was given to him and a village named in Isaiah's north-to-south march imagery; its site near [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) is uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain village in the Benjamin-Jerusalem area

locationsMap.name: Gamad
locationsMap.title: uncertain place or people linked with [Tyre](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000226)'s defenders
locationsMap.description: Gamad is a difficult geographic entry drawn from the Gammadim of [Ezekiel 27:11](verse-key://EZK 27:11), who served in [Tyre](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000226)'s towers; whether the word names a people from a place or means warriors is uncertain, so no firm site can be assigned.

locationsMap.name: Gareb
locationsMap.title: [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) boundary hill in Jeremiah's restoration oracle
locationsMap.description: Gareb was a hill or point on [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)'s future boundary in [Jeremiah 31:39](verse-key://JER 31:39); the passage locates it near Jerusalem, but the exact hill is unknown.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain hill or boundary point in Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Gate of Benjamin
locationsMap.title: [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) gate facing [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef)'s territory
locationsMap.description: The Gate of Benjamin was a [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) gate named in prophetic and narrative texts, apparently on the north or northeast side of the city toward [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef); its precise location is uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain northern or northeastern gate area of ancient Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Gate of Ephraim
locationsMap.title: [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) gate named for the road toward [Ephraim](location-id://0e95bdcb-42ff-4f2a-80d7-00c32ac05b2c)
locationsMap.description: The Gate of Ephraim was a [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) gate on the northern or northwestern wall, named for [Ephraim](location-id://0e95bdcb-42ff-4f2a-80d7-00c32ac05b2c) and appearing in wall and festival descriptions; its exact position is uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain northern or northwestern sector of ancient Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Gate of Yeshanah
locationsMap.title: [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) gate also rendered the Old Gate
locationsMap.description: The Gate of Yeshanah is the gate commonly rendered the Old Gate in KJV Nehemiah; it belonged to [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)'s rebuilt wall, but its exact placement is uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain gate of ancient Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Gate of the Foundation
locationsMap.title: temple-area gate assigned in [Jehoiada](name-id://f9531643-dfa4-4c2e-a5cc-cd2ddad755e7)'s guard plan
locationsMap.description: The Gate of the Foundation was one of the gates assigned to guards in [Jehoiada](name-id://f9531643-dfa4-4c2e-a5cc-cd2ddad755e7)'s arrangement during [Joash](name-id://5b36b473-4fab-405e-9776-716f92f0b62f)'s accession; the text places it in the temple-palace complex, but its exact location is unknown.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain gate in the Jerusalem temple-palace complex

locationsMap.name: Gate of the Guard
locationsMap.title: [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) gate in [Nehemiah](name-id://46c4c07f-dde8-4466-a278-6e40a8d3e7f1)'s procession list
locationsMap.description: The Gate of the Guard is a rendering of the gate called the Prison Gate in the KJV procession around [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)'s wall; its exact location on the wall is uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain gate of ancient Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Gathhepher
locationsMap.title: Zebulun town and birthplace of [Jonah](name-id://ca68bc73-d617-4010-8c81-4cfff8cc650c)
locationsMap.description: Gath-hepher was a town in Zebulun on the border list and the home of the prophet [Jonah](name-id://ca68bc73-d617-4010-8c81-4cfff8cc650c); it is commonly identified near el-Meshhed north of [Nazareth](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000167).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: el-Meshhed near Nazareth in northern Israel

locationsMap.name: Gathrimmon
locationsMap.title: Danite Levitical city also called Gath-rimmon
locationsMap.description: Gath-rimmon in [Dan](location-id://dadc79b1-e84f-40e0-ab31-2fa96b6ed4bd) was a Levitical city listed with Danite towns; it is distinct from the [Manasseh](name-id://6d826bc2-ac80-4c27-af89-258a50f37dfe)-associated Gath-rimmon in [Joshua 21:25](verse-key://JOS 21:25).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Often placed near Tell Gerisa or the Jaffa plain, but the identification remains uncertain

locationsMap.name: Geba
locationsMap.title: [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) city at the northern limit of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)'s reforms
locationsMap.description: Geba was a Benjaminite and Levitical city, often paired with [Gibeah](location-id://41084ab0-6cbc-4232-a844-fb8b405d97c3) and [Michmash](location-id://ee19b0f3-9647-4ed1-9f48-d9bef91d04fd) and used as a northern boundary marker; it is generally identified with modern Jaba northeast of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Jaba northeast of Jerusalem in the West Bank

locationsMap.name: Gebal
locationsMap.title: Phoenician Gebal, the city known to Greeks as Byblos
locationsMap.description: Gebal in [1 Kings](book-key://1KI) and [Ezekiel](book-key://EZK) was the Phoenician coastal city whose craftsmen were famous in timber and ship work; it is the same city later known as Byblos, distinct from the Gebal named with [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064) in [Psalm 83](chapter-key://PSA 83).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Byblos, Lebanon

locationsMap.name: Gebim
locationsMap.title: uncertain village in Isaiah's approach-to-[Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) oracle
locationsMap.description: Gebim was a village named in Isaiah's poetic march toward [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117), probably in [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) north of the city, but its exact site is unknown.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain village north of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Geder
locationsMap.title: Canaanite royal city in [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816)'s conquest list
locationsMap.description: Geder was a Canaanite royal city named among the kings defeated by [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816); the site has not been securely identified.

locationsMap.name: Gederah
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) lowland town in the Shephelah list
locationsMap.description: Gederah was a town in the lowland district of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and is also reflected in the gentilic Gederathite; it is often sought in the Shephelah, but exact identification is not certain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Possibly Khirbet Jadireh or another Shephelah site

locationsMap.name: Gederothaim
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) town name possibly duplicated from [Gederah](location-id://032c5b9b-8bcd-42fe-ad99-cc144529b3fd)
locationsMap.description: Gederothaim appears in [Joshua 15:36](verse-key://JOS 15:36) among [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)'s Shephelah towns, but the count in the verse has led many interpreters to suspect a textual duplication related to [Gederah](location-id://032c5b9b-8bcd-42fe-ad99-cc144529b3fd); no independent site is secure.

locationsMap.name: Gederoth
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) Shephelah town later taken by Philistines
locationsMap.description: Gederoth was a town in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)'s lowland district and one of the places taken by Philistines in [Ahaz](name-id://6c49dd1b-6675-4393-9df4-46e7ab71be60)'s day; it is probably in the Shephelah, but the exact site is uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain Shephelah site, sometimes connected with Katrah or Gedera traditions

locationsMap.name: Gedor
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) hill-country town and uncertain Simeonite reading
locationsMap.description: Gedor was a town in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119); the Gedor of [1 Chronicles 4:39](verse-key://1CH 4:39) may preserve a difficult or variant reading, so the precise geography of that reference is uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Often associated with Khirbet Jedur in the Judah hill country, but not certain

locationsMap.name: Geliloth
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)-[Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) boundary point near [Adummim](location-id://147db671-a765-4d7f-b250-b6614116bef2)
locationsMap.description: Geliloth was a boundary point between [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) over against the ascent of [Adummim](location-id://147db671-a765-4d7f-b250-b6614116bef2); it may preserve a form related to [Gilgal](location-id://5d536a42-83f6-4caf-8fb3-c11de63ca7de), but it is not securely identified with a known site.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain boundary point near the ascent of Adummim east of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Gennesaret
locationsMap.title: fertile plain beside the [Sea of Galilee](location-id://44329b87-3c5b-4d27-9fcf-e386f2aebc5b)
locationsMap.description: Gennesaret was the fertile plain on the northwest side of the [Sea of Galilee](location-id://44329b87-3c5b-4d27-9fcf-e386f2aebc5b) and also gave its name to the lake in [Luke 5:1](verse-key://LUK 5:1).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Plain of Gennesaret on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee

locationsMap.name: Geshur
locationsMap.title: Aramean kingdom or district northeast of [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d)
locationsMap.description: Geshur was a small Aramean kingdom or territory near [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d) and the upper [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) region, connected with [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) through Maacah and [Absalom](name-id://0e94a17b-69b1-4148-b7de-72eab8eea4cc); its borders are approximate.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Region of the southern Golan and adjoining southern Syria

locationsMap.name: Gezer
locationsMap.title: fortified Canaanite city on the road from coast to highlands
locationsMap.description: Gezer was a major Canaanite and Israelite city controlling routes between the coastal plain and hill country; it is securely identified with Tel Gezer.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Gezer in central Israel

locationsMap.name: Giah
locationsMap.title: uncertain point on [Abner](name-id://3ce44295-3e16-47da-9037-8888f703aae7)'s route near [Gibeon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000088)
locationsMap.description: Giah was a place on the route by the wilderness of [Gibeon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000088) during [Abner](name-id://3ce44295-3e16-47da-9037-8888f703aae7)'s retreat; the text gives only a relative location, and the site is not known.

locationsMap.name: Gibbethon
locationsMap.title: Danite Levitical city contested by Israel and Philistines
locationsMap.description: Gibbethon was a city allotted in [Dan](location-id://dadc79b1-e84f-40e0-ab31-2fa96b6ed4bd) and given to the Levites, later held or besieged by Philistines during Israel's monarchy; its site is uncertain.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain site in the Danite or Philistine border region

locationsMap.name: Gibeah
locationsMap.title: Gibeah of [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef), [Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb)'s city and scene of [Judges 19](chapter-key://JDG 19)-20
locationsMap.description: Gibeah of [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) was the Benjaminite city central to the outrage and war in [Judges](book-key://JDG) and later associated with [Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb); it is commonly identified with Tell el-Ful north of [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tell el-Ful north of Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Gidom
locationsMap.title: [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) place reached by fleeing survivors
locationsMap.description: Gidom was a place in [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) reached in the battle narrative after the destruction of [Gibeah](location-id://41084ab0-6cbc-4232-a844-fb8b405d97c3); its location is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Gihon
locationsMap.title: [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) spring where [Solomon](name-id://509b7c2f-b8bf-4a4d-a393-550a7a4b259f) was anointed
locationsMap.description: Gihon is the spring on [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117)'s eastern slope where [Solomon](name-id://509b7c2f-b8bf-4a4d-a393-550a7a4b259f) was anointed and whose waters [Hezekiah](name-id://9854b257-50aa-4284-8f7b-84351d2b226f) later diverted; it is distinct from the Gihon river of Eden in [Genesis 2](chapter-key://GEN 2).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Gihon Spring in the City of David, Jerusalem

locationsMap.name: Gilboa
locationsMap.title: mountain range where Saul fell in battle
locationsMap.description: Gilboa was the mountain or range overlooking the Jezreel Valley where [Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb) and his sons died after battle with the Philistines.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Mount Gilboa range in northern Israel

locationsMap.name: Gilgal
locationsMap.title: Israel's camp near [Jericho](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000116) after crossing the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987)
locationsMap.description: Gilgal near [Jericho](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000116) was Israel's first camp west of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987), the place of memorial stones, circumcision, Passover, and many later [Samuel](name-id://1f1722fd-38b9-474c-9c94-fcbeb1d47812)-[Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb) traditions; it is distinct from the [Bethel](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000032)-area Gilgal and the Gilgal of the Nations.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain site east of Jericho in the Jordan Valley

locationsMap.name: Giloh
locationsMap.title: [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) hill-country town associated with [Ahithophel](name-id://f68eb2e9-a4d7-473d-99d1-74ff363fa7ee)
locationsMap.description: Giloh was a town in the hill country of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and the home city of [Ahithophel](name-id://f68eb2e9-a4d7-473d-99d1-74ff363fa7ee) the Gilonite; the shorter form Gilo is treated here as an alias rather than a separate place.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain site in the Judah hill country, often placed southwest of Hebron

locationsMap.name: Gimzo
locationsMap.title: lowland town captured by Philistines in [Ahaz](name-id://6c49dd1b-6675-4393-9df4-46e7ab71be60)'s reign
locationsMap.description: Gimzo was a town in the lowland district of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) taken by Philistines during the reign of [Ahaz](name-id://6c49dd1b-6675-4393-9df4-46e7ab71be60); it is commonly identified with Jimzu.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Jimzu in central Israel

locationsMap.name: Gittaim
locationsMap.title: [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef) settlement associated with Beerothite refugees
locationsMap.description: Gittaim was a [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef)-area settlement where Beerothite families sojourned and later a postexilic town; its exact location is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Gob
locationsMap.title: textually uncertain battle site in [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)'s wars
locationsMap.description: Gob appears in [2 Samuel 21](chapter-key://2SA 21) as the site of battles with Philistine giants, but the parallel in Chronicles reads [Gezer](location-id://a5481946-ed06-43e0-8ed1-c4ed123a26f5), so the place may reflect a textual variant rather than a separately identifiable site.

locationsMap.name: Golan
locationsMap.title: city of refuge in [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d) allotted to [Manasseh](name-id://6d826bc2-ac80-4c27-af89-258a50f37dfe)'s Levites
locationsMap.description: Golan was the city of refuge in [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d) and a Levitical city from the half-tribe of [Manasseh](name-id://6d826bc2-ac80-4c27-af89-258a50f37dfe); its precise ancient site is uncertain within the Golan or Jaulan region.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain site in the Golan or Jaulan region east of the Sea of Galilee

locationsMap.name: Gozan
locationsMap.title: Assyrian exile region on or near the [Habor](location-id://b1b043d5-56dd-4d9f-a2fe-0f32cc2649e0)
locationsMap.description: Gozan was a Mesopotamian region or river district where [Assyria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000023) settled Israelite exiles, repeatedly named with [Habor](location-id://b1b043d5-56dd-4d9f-a2fe-0f32cc2649e0) and the cities of the Medes.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Khabur River region of upper Mesopotamia, especially northeastern Syria and southeastern Turkey

locationsMap.name: Great Sidon
locationsMap.title: KJV boundary phrase for the city of [Sidon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000208)
locationsMap.description: Great Sidon, KJV Great Zidon, refers to the prominent Phoenician city of [Sidon](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000208) in [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816)'s northern campaign boundary; it is the same city as Sidon rather than a separate site.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Sidon, Lebanon

locationsMap.name: Gudgodah
locationsMap.title: wilderness station near [Jotbath](location-id://72a38431-42c2-4ad8-8b90-0cf5eec8f457) in [Moses](name-id://fff825ad-31e8-4843-a7dc-cd82e9878d73)' itinerary
locationsMap.description: Gudgodah was a wilderness stopping place named between Beeroth of the children of Jaakan and [Jotbath](location-id://72a38431-42c2-4ad8-8b90-0cf5eec8f457); its location is uncertain and may correspond to Hor-hagidgad in [Numbers 33](chapter-key://NUM 33).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain wilderness station, commonly sought in the Arabah or southern wilderness route

locationsMap.name: Gurbaal
locationsMap.title: Arabian place subdued in [Uzziah](name-id://a463bd46-3fbc-418b-9809-a0f157b942ea)'s campaign
locationsMap.description: Gurbaal was a place or district of Arabs subdued by [Uzziah](name-id://a463bd46-3fbc-418b-9809-a0f157b942ea), named with the Mehunims; its site is uncertain, often sought in the [Edom](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000064)-Arabian borderlands.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain place in the southern Transjordan or northwestern Arabian region

locationsMap.name: Gur
locationsMap.title: ascent by [Ibleam](location-id://78607a80-3155-437a-aeeb-70f7f1ca66fe) where Ahaziah fled
locationsMap.description: Gur was the ascent or road by [Ibleam](location-id://78607a80-3155-437a-aeeb-70f7f1ca66fe) where Ahaziah was struck while fleeing [Jehu](name-id://f3fdd9d6-b20c-4fd4-80a5-63258fba4c9f); it is tied to Ibleam but not independently located with certainty.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Uncertain ascent near Ibleam in the Jezreel-Samaria border area

locationsMap.name: Gad
locationsMap.title: Transjordan tribal territory in [Gilead](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000089) east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987)
locationsMap.description: Gad was the tribal territory [Moses](name-id://fff825ad-31e8-4843-a7dc-cd82e9878d73) allotted to the descendants of [Jacob](name-id://23ed64d8-8458-49af-9b51-f578ab3262d9)’s son [Gad](name-id://b68edd6a-6aea-4f9f-8c99-684d9a6f7a8b), lying in [Gilead](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000089) east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) about the [Jabbok](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000111), where its people built [Dibon](location-id://66711495-33a2-4df0-89e5-ad3a2c12c9f0), [Ataroth](location-id://02588d46-c5ba-4c85-9982-ae79a3a79b8d), and [Aroer](location-id://7e8f3dee-29fd-4046-8dbf-60833db11548), and where [Mahanaim](location-id://67203862-b8e5-482c-b736-3f4120ba8397) stood as a chief city. Centuries later [Jeremiah](name-id://3a62ca29-870f-4a9b-844b-887f828a0cd5) asked why the king of the Ammonites should inherit Gad.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: north-central Jordan between the Wadi Mujib and the Ajlun highlands

locationsMap.name: Haran
locationsMap.title: Mesopotamian city where [Terah](name-id://1eb1d1a1-b9a2-4b87-90b3-b50fc200376d) settled and [Abram](name-id://bf42c58c-045a-4131-b8ee-55e7c707040a) departed for [Canaan](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000045)
locationsMap.description: Haran was the city in [Mesopotamia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000151) where [Terah](name-id://1eb1d1a1-b9a2-4b87-90b3-b50fc200376d)'s household settled after leaving Ur and from which [Abram](name-id://bf42c58c-045a-4131-b8ee-55e7c707040a) later departed toward [Canaan](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000045); it is also associated with [Laban](name-id://02b09a01-9819-4182-895a-b0dda2395250) and with later prophetic references to northern Mesopotamian trade and Assyrian conquest.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Harran in Sanliurfa Province, Turkey

locationsMap.name: Havilah
locationsMap.title: gold-bearing land encircled by Pison in the Eden geography
locationsMap.description: Havilah in [Genesis 2](chapter-key://GEN 2) is the land said to be compassed by the river Pison and noted for gold, bdellium, and onyx stone; its location is not securely identified and should be distinguished from the later desert Havilah associated with [Ishmael](name-id://056fd84a-3a55-4428-aef2-584809d7d7b1) and [Amalek](name-id://04a074df-ec7b-4d3b-9f86-b3cb1d6cdd51).

locationsMap.name: Hazezontamar
locationsMap.title: KJV [Genesis](book-key://GEN) spelling of [Hazazontamar](location-id://01cbbee4-41b6-442f-a7c1-a64c15f9542f), identified with [Engedi](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000070)
locationsMap.description: Hazezontamar is the King James spelling in [Genesis 14:7](verse-key://GEN 14:7) for the place reached by [Chedorlaomer](name-id://ed428395-dc41-4ed2-9229-bd7abfaa930f)'s coalition after smiting the Amalekites and Amorites; [2 Chronicles 20:2](verse-key://2CH 20:2) spells the name Hazazontamar and identifies it with [Engedi](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000070).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ein Gedi on the western shore of the Dead Sea

locationsMap.name: Hebron
locationsMap.title: patriarchal hill-country city of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)'s first capital
locationsMap.description: Hebron, formerly called Kirjath-arba, was a major hill-country city in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) associated with [Abraham](name-id://4ce14dfc-b652-45d9-ac05-5f0cf716c412), [Sarah](name-id://3b881f0a-320a-4065-ba4e-aae92ee71d34), [Caleb](name-id://2e9a92f4-f47e-4243-b5d1-5c0f7d746456), the Anakim, the Levitical city of refuge, and [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)'s seven-and-a-half-year reign before [Jerusalem](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000117) became his capital.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Hebron in the southern West Bank

locationsMap.name: Helam
locationsMap.title: place where [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) defeated the Syrians beyond the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987)
locationsMap.description: Helam was the place where the Syrians gathered after [Hadarezer](name-id://efa8c76a-4d8a-4b15-af7f-079ee3c25957) sent reinforcements from beyond the river, and where [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) crossed [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) and defeated them; its exact site is not securely identified.

locationsMap.name: Hill of Gaash
locationsMap.title: hill near [Timnathserah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000222) where [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816) was buried
locationsMap.description: The hill of Gaash (KJV "the hill of Gaash", [Joshua 24:30](verse-key://JOS 24:30); "the hill Gaash", [Judges 2:9](verse-key://JDG 2:9)) was the landmark named in [Joshua](name-id://28e270de-d886-42b6-918b-665be906a816)'s burial notice, on the north side of [Timnathserah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000222) in Mount Ephraim; its exact site is not securely identified apart from that association.

locationsMap.name: Habor
locationsMap.title: river of [Gozan](location-id://2523eaa0-fc28-41ef-99bb-aa3ab91569b1) where Israelites were settled in exile
locationsMap.description: Habor was the river of [Gozan](location-id://2523eaa0-fc28-41ef-99bb-aa3ab91569b1) named among the places where the Assyrians settled Israelites from [Samaria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000196) and the trans-Jordanian tribes; it is commonly identified with the Khabur River system in northern [Mesopotamia](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000151).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Khabur River region in northeastern Syria and southeastern Turkey

locationsMap.name: Hachilah
locationsMap.title: hill in the wilderness of [Ziph](location-id://212b3b0d-07c7-4506-99f7-2bd90c1942ce) where [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c) hid from [Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb)
locationsMap.description: Hachilah was the hill beside [Jeshimon](location-id://d74d6fe1-9804-4be0-90e1-819aa4d70eb5) in the wilderness of [Ziph](location-id://212b3b0d-07c7-4506-99f7-2bd90c1942ce) where the Ziphites reported [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)'s hiding place to [Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb) and where David later spared Saul in the camp; the exact hill is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Hadadrimmon
locationsMap.title: place in the valley of Megiddon remembered for mourning
locationsMap.description: Hadadrimmon is named in [Zechariah](book-key://ZEC) as the comparison for a great mourning in the valley of Megiddon; it is often connected with a site near [Megiddo](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000148), but the identification remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Hadashah
locationsMap.title: Shephelah town in the inheritance of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Hadashah was a town listed among the lowland cities of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) in [Joshua 15](chapter-key://JOS 15); Scripture gives no further detail, and its exact site is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Hadid
locationsMap.title: postexilic town near [Lod](location-id://3489d177-3d3f-42b0-91da-f3ce024c9316) and [Ono](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000172)
locationsMap.description: Hadid was a town named with [Lod](location-id://3489d177-3d3f-42b0-91da-f3ce024c9316) and [Ono](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000172) among the returned exiles and later among the settlements of [Benjamin](location-id://80f2867e-4e7c-43b6-aa11-7fd42550d4ef); it is commonly identified with Tel Hadid near the Ayalon Valley.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Hadid near modern Ben Shemen, Israel

locationsMap.name: Hadrach
locationsMap.title: northern Syrian land named with [Damascus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000061) in [Zechariah](book-key://ZEC)
locationsMap.description: Hadrach is named in Zechariah's oracle with [Damascus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000061) and [Hamath](location-id://e88700f4-7b74-49f1-bf22-d4a4a6992b62). It is usually understood as a northern Syrian district or city, but the precise biblical identification remains debated.

locationsMap.name: Halah
locationsMap.title: Assyrian exile location named with [Habor](location-id://b1b043d5-56dd-4d9f-a2fe-0f32cc2649e0) and [Gozan](location-id://2523eaa0-fc28-41ef-99bb-aa3ab91569b1)
locationsMap.description: Halah was one of the places where the Assyrians carried Israelites from [Samaria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000196) and the trans-Jordanian tribes; its exact location is uncertain, though it is named with [Habor](location-id://b1b043d5-56dd-4d9f-a2fe-0f32cc2649e0), [Gozan](location-id://2523eaa0-fc28-41ef-99bb-aa3ab91569b1), and the cities of the Medes.

locationsMap.name: Halhul
locationsMap.title: hill-country town of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) north of [Hebron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000103)
locationsMap.description: Halhul was a town in the hill-country allotment of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119), listed with Bethzur and [Gedor](location-id://12785454-38f5-42d6-ba3c-aae15b5174ff); it preserves its ancient name in the modern town of Halhul near [Hebron](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000103).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Halhul north of Hebron in the southern West Bank

locationsMap.name: Hali
locationsMap.title: Asherite town named in the western [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080) allotment
locationsMap.description: Hali was a town listed in the inheritance of [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797) between [Helkath](location-id://98dbbcc8-86a4-4c79-a8c6-eaf1d34d0cc2) and Beten; the biblical notice is brief and no secure modern identification is known.

locationsMap.name: Ham
locationsMap.title: place where [Chedorlaomer](name-id://ed428395-dc41-4ed2-9229-bd7abfaa930f) defeated the Zuzims
locationsMap.description: Ham was the place where [Chedorlaomer](name-id://ed428395-dc41-4ed2-9229-bd7abfaa930f) and his allies smote the Zuzims in [Genesis 14](chapter-key://GEN 14); it is distinct from the poetic phrase land of Ham for [Egypt](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000065), and its exact site is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Hamath
locationsMap.title: Syrian city and kingdom on the Orontes marking Israel's northern reach
locationsMap.description: Hamath was a major city and kingdom on the Orontes River, repeatedly named as a northern landmark for Israel and [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and as a Syrian power involved in Assyrian and Babylonian-era history.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Hama, Syria

locationsMap.name: Hamathzobah
locationsMap.title: region conquered by [Solomon](name-id://509b7c2f-b8bf-4a4d-a393-550a7a4b259f) and linked with [Hamath](location-id://e88700f4-7b74-49f1-bf22-d4a4a6992b62) and [Zobah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000246)
locationsMap.description: Hamathzobah is named in Chronicles as the place or region [Solomon](name-id://509b7c2f-b8bf-4a4d-a393-550a7a4b259f) went against and prevailed over; the compound links [Hamath](location-id://e88700f4-7b74-49f1-bf22-d4a4a6992b62) with [Zobah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000246), but the precise territory intended is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Hammath
locationsMap.title: fortified [Naphtali](name-id://e8c79c45-33b0-4b1e-9265-368c54b9604a) town by the hot springs near [Chinnereth](location-id://d4a473b2-abb9-4856-bebe-fb0294b0e071)
locationsMap.description: Hammath was one of the fenced cities of [Naphtali](name-id://e8c79c45-33b0-4b1e-9265-368c54b9604a) listed with Rakkath and [Chinnereth](location-id://d4a473b2-abb9-4856-bebe-fb0294b0e071); it is commonly associated with the hot-spring site of Hamat [Tiberias](location-id://8e5502fe-336a-4263-b9a2-2f31ee57e754) by the [Sea of Galilee](location-id://44329b87-3c5b-4d27-9fcf-e386f2aebc5b).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Hamat Tiberias by Tiberias, Israel

locationsMap.name: Hammon
locationsMap.title: Asherite town named on the northern coastal border
locationsMap.description: Hammon in [Joshua](book-key://JOS) is a town in [Asher](name-id://7999131a-6b35-4c3c-96f5-7f71d4d7c797)'s allotment listed between [Kanah](location-id://8b15378d-6483-4517-ac24-756d86f08fe8) and Zidon; the name in [1 Chronicles](book-key://1CH) likely points to the [Naphtali](name-id://e8c79c45-33b0-4b1e-9265-368c54b9604a) Levitical city also called [Hammothdor](location-id://89869b3b-2ebc-4500-8fc6-4c0df3bb6165), so this record keeps the Asher town separate.

locationsMap.name: Hammothdor
locationsMap.title: Levitical city of [Naphtali](name-id://e8c79c45-33b0-4b1e-9265-368c54b9604a) also associated with [Hammath](location-id://15138706-7da3-4893-8388-42f6a8876504)
locationsMap.description: Hammothdor was a Levitical city allotted from [Naphtali](name-id://e8c79c45-33b0-4b1e-9265-368c54b9604a) to the Gershonites; it is generally treated as the same hot-spring site as [Hammath](location-id://15138706-7da3-4893-8388-42f6a8876504), later Hamat [Tiberias](location-id://8e5502fe-336a-4263-b9a2-2f31ee57e754).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Hamat Tiberias by Tiberias, Israel

locationsMap.name: Hamonah
locationsMap.title: city named in Ezekiel's burial vision for Gog's multitude
locationsMap.description: Hamonah is the city name given in Ezekiel's vision after the burial of Gog's multitude in the valley of Hamon-gog; because the passage is prophetic and symbolic, no secure modern location is identifiable.

locationsMap.name: Hanes
locationsMap.title: Egyptian city reached by [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)'s envoys in [Isaiah](book-key://ISA)
locationsMap.description: Hanes was an Egyptian city named with [Zoan](location-id://e2cd68a5-58cb-4151-92ea-342beeb5f9be) as the destination of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)'s princes seeking help from [Egypt](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000065); it is commonly identified with Heracleopolis Magna, though the biblical notice is brief.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ihnasya el-Medina, the site of Heracleopolis Magna in Egypt

locationsMap.name: Hannathon
locationsMap.title: Zebulun border town near the valley of Jiphthah-el
locationsMap.description: Hannathon was a town on Zebulun's boundary before the line reached the valley of Jiphthah-el; it is commonly associated with Tel Hanaton in lower [Galilee](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000080).
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Tel Hanaton in Lower Galilee, Israel

locationsMap.name: Haradah
locationsMap.title: Israelite wilderness encampment between Mount Shepher and Makheloth
locationsMap.description: Haradah was one of the wilderness stations in [Numbers 33](chapter-key://NUM 33), reached after Mount Shepher and followed by Makheloth; its exact location on the route is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Hara
locationsMap.title: Assyrian exile location named with [Halah](location-id://c0699235-caa5-4823-b936-b81b114de79e) and [Habor](location-id://b1b043d5-56dd-4d9f-a2fe-0f32cc2649e0)
locationsMap.description: Hara is named in Chronicles among the places where [Tiglath-pileser](name-id://2db142f3-68a9-4a69-9853-b95e20811302) carried the Reubenites, Gadites, and half tribe of [Manasseh](name-id://6d826bc2-ac80-4c27-af89-258a50f37dfe); its exact location is uncertain and may refer to a region connected with [Halah](location-id://c0699235-caa5-4823-b936-b81b114de79e), [Habor](location-id://b1b043d5-56dd-4d9f-a2fe-0f32cc2649e0), and [Gozan](location-id://2523eaa0-fc28-41ef-99bb-aa3ab91569b1).

locationsMap.name: Harod
locationsMap.title: spring where [Gideon](name-id://c639ae62-acde-4142-a3f5-fd40204fc455) camped before fighting Midian
locationsMap.description: Harod is the spring or well where [Gideon](name-id://c639ae62-acde-4142-a3f5-fd40204fc455) and Israel camped before the battle with Midian; later references to Harodites connect [David](name-id://0e06ff0e-0ca5-4f9f-9a3b-874f91497f7c)'s warriors with the same place-name tradition in the Jezreel region.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: Ain Jalut or the spring of Harod near Mount Gilboa, Israel

locationsMap.name: Hashmonah
locationsMap.title: Israelite wilderness encampment between Mithcah and Moseroth
locationsMap.description: Hashmonah was one of Israel's wilderness stations in [Numbers 33](chapter-key://NUM 33), reached after Mithcah and followed by Moseroth; its exact location is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Hauran
locationsMap.title: southern Syrian region named on Ezekiel's ideal northern border
locationsMap.description: Hauran was the region east of the [Jordan](location-id://ac7e67b8-98a6-49fa-a8fd-6437b333b987) and south of [Damascus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000061) included in Ezekiel's description of the land's northern and eastern boundary; it corresponds broadly to the volcanic plateau of southern Syria and northern Jordan.
locationsMap.modernIdentification: The Hauran region of southern Syria and northern Jordan

locationsMap.name: Havilah of Ishmael and Amalek
locationsMap.title: desert region on the route toward [Shur](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000207) and [Assyria](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000023)
locationsMap.description: This Havilah is the region associated with [Ishmael](name-id://056fd84a-3a55-4428-aef2-584809d7d7b1)'s descendants and with [Saul](name-id://7dbe7bce-7888-4b8f-8804-c9910bb04fcb)'s campaign against [Amalek](name-id://04a074df-ec7b-4d3b-9f86-b3cb1d6cdd51) from Havilah toward [Shur](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000207); it is distinct from the Eden-region Havilah of [Genesis 2](chapter-key://GEN 2) and remains geographically uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Havothjair
locationsMap.title: villages of [Jair](name-id://5cc03ebd-cc1f-4cba-8140-f002651a9d10) in [Gilead](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000089) and [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d)
locationsMap.description: Havothjair, meaning the villages or tent-villages of [Jair](name-id://5cc03ebd-cc1f-4cba-8140-f002651a9d10), were settlements taken and named by Jair in the region of [Gilead](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000089) and [Bashan](location-id://af0d12bf-aa1c-494c-9f89-8288fd65ef3d); the biblical notices connect them with [Manasseh](name-id://6d826bc2-ac80-4c27-af89-258a50f37dfe) and with later judgeship traditions.

locationsMap.name: Hazaraddar
locationsMap.title: southern boundary point of the promised land near Kadesh
locationsMap.description: Hazaraddar was a place on the southern boundary line in [Numbers 34](chapter-key://NUM 34), named after the border turned from Kadesh toward Azmon; its exact site is unknown.

locationsMap.name: Hazarenan
locationsMap.title: northern boundary point named in [Numbers](book-key://NUM) and [Ezekiel](book-key://EZK)
locationsMap.description: Hazarenan was a boundary point at the northern reach of the land in [Numbers](book-key://NUM) and [Ezekiel](book-key://EZK), named with the way to [Hamath](location-id://e88700f4-7b74-49f1-bf22-d4a4a6992b62) and the border of [Damascus](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000061); its exact identification remains uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Hazargaddah
locationsMap.title: Negeb town in the inheritance of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)
locationsMap.description: Hazargaddah was a town listed in the southern or Negeb district of [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)'s inheritance; the biblical list gives no further detail and the site is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Hazarshual
locationsMap.title: southern town assigned to [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119) and [Simeon](name-id://cca9437f-0046-4dd6-a7eb-45ac460a161a) and resettled after exile
locationsMap.description: Hazarshual was a Negeb town listed in [Judah](location-id://00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000119)'s inheritance, assigned also within [Simeon](name-id://cca9437f-0046-4dd6-a7eb-45ac460a161a)'s territory, and later named among postexilic settlements; its exact modern identification is uncertain.

locationsMap.name: Hazarsusah
locationsMap.title: Simeonite town also represented by [Hazarsusim](location-id://6650345d-0ee7-435d-a833-800fcbbe7a6b)
locationsMap.description: Hazarsusah was a town in [Simeon](name-id://cca9437f-0046-4dd6-a7eb-45ac460a161a)'s inheritance, and the parallel form [Hazarsusim](location-id://6650345d-0ee7-435d-a833-800fcbbe7a6b) appears in Chronicles; both names probably refer to the same horse-village site, but the location is uncertain.
